items.title: Punjab govt bans use, sale of camera-enabled smart glasses, devices with hidden recording ability for 30 days
items.description: The Punjab government issued an order on Tuesday banning the use and sale of camera-enabled smart glasses and “miniature cameras with recording ability disguised as everyday objects” within the province for 30 days. The restriction was notified in an order by the Punjab Home Department, in exercise of powers conferred under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. “No person shall wear or operate ‘camera-enabled smart glasses with hidden recording ability’ OR ‘miniature cameras with recording ability disguised as everyday objects such as pen, keychain, etc.’,” the order said, adding that the restriction excluded laptops, handheld tablets, mobile phones and terminal equipment approved by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority. In addition, it restricted retailers, wholesale dealers, traders and distributors from selling or offering these devices for sale, “online or off the shelf”. The order noted that it had been reported that the unrestricted use of these glasses and disguised cameras — capable of “capturing, processing and transmitting data in the form of speech, images, videos and sound” — in Punjab could pose a “serious risk” to public order, individual privacy, particularly the “integrity and dignity” of women and children; security of sensitive data and installations; and institutional integrity. It named airports, examination centres, secure government establishments, healthcare facilities, shopping malls, court premises and public places as particular areas of risk. The order also noted that these activities were deemed to “create an imminent apprehension of secret recording, breach of privacy and security, or unauthorised transmission of protected information”. “Immediate preventive action is necessary to ensure public safety, integrity and dignity of persons particularly women and children, and the maintenance of order within the province,” it stated. The order said the ban was being enforced with immediate effect and will remain in force for a period of 30 days unless withdrawn earlier. It was also specified that “authorised law enforcement personnel” would be exempt from the restriction. Amid concerns about the misuse of such devices, the Lahore High Court (LHC) has also been seized with a public interest petition that challenges the unregulated import and sale of camera and mic-equipped smart glasses, citing threats to people’s privacy, dignity and national security. Meta in particular has faced pushback for its AI-powered smart glasses, with critics dubbing the eyewear as “pervert glasses”. And while it has not officially listed Pakistan as a market, the petitioner’s counsel in the case before the LHC has contended that its glasses are openly sold online and in shops in Lahore. Taking up the plea on Thursday, the LHC directed the federal government to forward a summary to the federal cabinet regarding the unregulated import and sale of smart glasses.

items.title: Sanwo-Olu mourns Fasoranti, says end of era
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor and Chairman of the South-West Governors’ Forum, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has mourned the death of the leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing his passing as the end of an era. Fasoranti, a respected elder statesman and educationist, died on Tuesday at the age of 100. Sanwo-Olu, in a condolence message he personally signed, described his death as a major loss to the Yoruba people and Nigeria. “On behalf of my family, the Government and people of Lagos State, as well as my brother Governors in the South-West, I commiserate with the Fasoranti family, Afenifere members and the entire people of Yorubaland over the departure of our respected leader and elder statesman, Pa Reuben Fasoranti,” he said. The governor described the late Afenifere leader as a committed statesman and a symbol of wisdom, integrity and selfless service who devoted himself to the advancement of the Yoruba people and Nigeria. “Baba Fasoranti was a respected and passionate statesman whose contributions to education, leadership and public service remain indelible. He impacted many lives positively through courageous and uncompromising leadership. His commitment to public service and community development was commendable,” Sanwo-Olu said. He extended his condolences to his Ondo State counterpart, Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa; the government and people of Ondo State, particularly the Akure Kingdom; the Fasoranti family; and members of Afenifere. Sanwo-Olu said Fasoranti made significant contributions to Yorubaland and Nigeria during his lifetime, particularly through his leadership of Afenifere. “Pa Fasoranti during his lifetime made a lot of positive impact in Yorubaland and Nigeria. He did great exploits as leader of Afenifere by steering the ship of the pan-Yoruba socio-cultural organisation in the right direction. “We cherish Pa Fasoranti’s commitment to fighting for truth, equity, justice, true federalism and good governance, which he championed for many decades,” he added. The governor prayed for the repose of Fasoranti’s soul and for God to grant his family and the Yoruba people the strength to bear the loss. The post Sanwo-Olu mourns Fasoranti, says end of era appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ISSER calls for manufacturing-led growth to create jobs
items.description: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) is urging government to prioritise manufacturing, agricultural productivity and private-sector financing to translate Ghana’s economic growth into jobs and improved living standards. Director of ISSER, Professor Robert Darko Osei, says the country must focus on economic growth that generates employment and delivers tangible benefits to households. Speaking at the launch of the 2025 State of the Ghanaian Economy Report, he said stronger growth could accelerate improvements in incomes and economic opportunities. “I think it’s very simple. The one-liner is that we need to translate that into real jobs, real sector improvements,” Professor Osei said. He explained that increasing economic growth by two percentage points could reduce the time needed to double per capital gross domestic product (GDP) by about five years from the current estimate of 17 years. Professor Osei identified manufacturing as critical to job creation, warning against excessive reliance on raw material exports. “The growth effort, we cannot ignore. We need to consolidate and we need to improve it. But the type of growth also matters. Because point source, relying so much on point source resources such as gold cannot be sustainable,” he said. He also warned that government borrowing could limit access to credit for businesses seeking to expand. “If government continues to borrow, then the tendency is that it’s going to crowd out private credits,” he said. Meanwhile, Head of the Economics Division at ISSER, Professor Fred Dzanku, says declining inflation has not necessarily eased the cost-of-living burden on households. He noted that although inflation has fallen considerably, prices have not necessarily declined. “Even though inflation, which is measuring the rate of increase in prices, have reduced considerably, it doesn’t mean prices have fallen,” Professor Dzanku said. He explained that households could remain financially strained when their incomes fail to keep pace with rising prices, even as inflation slows. “What we need to do really is to see how do we increase the incomes of households. Because when your income increases, your disposable income increases, you are better able to afford the same commodity,” he added. Professor Dzanku stressed that the inability of consumers to afford goods and services remains a major concern. “That’s why people normally will say that we are not feeling it in our pocket, because they don’t have money,” he said. The ISSER report highlights the need to complement macroeconomic stability with job creation, productive investment and higher household incomes to ensure that economic recovery benefits businesses and ordinary Ghanaians.

items.title: Ebola Virus: 7 things to know about causes, symptoms, prevention
items.description: Ebola virus is a dangerous virus that causes Ebola virus disease (EVD), a serious infectious illness that can be fatal. The virus can spread from infected animals to humans and from one infected person to another through direct contact with infected blood and other bodily fluids. Ebola can cause fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. In severe cases, the disease can damage vital organs and cause bleeding. However, not everyone who contracts Ebola dies. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. Humans may become infected through contact with infected wild animals, including fruit bats, monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and other susceptible animals. Causes and symptoms of ebola Ebola virus disease is caused by infection with an Ebola virus. The disease can affect several parts of the body and may become severe without appropriate medical care. Symptoms usually appear between two and 21 days after exposure to the virus, although they often begin within eight to 10 days. Early symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, extreme weakness, tiredness, muscle and joint pain, sore throat and loss of appetite. As the disease progresses, other symptoms may develop, including vomiting, diarrhoea, severe abdominal pain and skin rash. Some patients may experience unexplained bruising or bleeding from the gums, nose or other parts of the body. In severe cases, Ebola can cause complications affecting the liver, kidneys and other vital organs. However, not everyone with Ebola experiences bleeding. Fever, headache and weakness alone do not necessarily indicate Ebola because malaria, Lassa fever and other illnesses can cause similar symptoms. Medical assessment and appropriate laboratory testing are necessary to establish the cause of the illness. How ebola spreads Ebola spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms. These fluids include vomit, stool, urine and other secretions that may contain the virus. A person can become infected when these fluids enter the body through broken skin or the eyes, nose or mouth. Family members and healthcare workers may be exposed when caring for infected patients without appropriate protective equipment. The virus can also spread through contaminated objects, such as needles, clothing, bedding and medical equipment, particularly when they contain infectious bodily fluids. Another significant source of transmission is the body of a person who has died from Ebola. The body may remain infectious, making traditional burial practices involving direct contact with the deceased particularly dangerous. Humans may also contract Ebola through contact with infected wild animals, including certain bats and non-human primates. Ebola does not ordinarily spread through the air like measles or influenza. Simply walking past an infected person, living in the same city or travelling on the same flight does not automatically mean that someone will contract the disease. The risk depends on the nature of the exposure. Generally, people infected with Ebola are not considered contagious before symptoms develop. Nevertheless, anyone who has had contact with a confirmed case should follow public health instructions and seek guidance from health authorities. What to do If you suspect ebola infection Anyone who suspects they may have contracted Ebola should seek urgent medical guidance and follow the instructions of public health authorities. The first step is to contact the relevant health authorities if symptoms develop after contact with a suspected or confirmed Ebola patient or following possible exposure in an area experiencing an outbreak. It is important to call a hospital or healthcare facility before visiting. Informing medical personnel about the symptoms and possible exposure allows them to make appropriate arrangements to receive the patient safely and reduce the risk of further transmission. While awaiting medical guidance, the suspected patient should avoid close contact with other people and should not share items that may be contaminated with bodily fluids. People who suspect Ebola infection should not attempt to treat themselves with traditional remedies or take medicines without medical guidance. The disease requires specialised medical assessment and care. Treatment may include providing fluids to prevent dehydration, correcting electrolyte imbalances, managing complications and supporting affected organs. Specific antibody treatments are available for certain types of Ebola virus disease. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can significantly improve the chances of survival. Prevention of ebola Preventive measures are essential for reducing the risk of Ebola infection, particularly during an outbreak. People should wash their hands regularly with soap and water and avoid contact with the blood and bodily fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola. They should also avoid touching the bodies of people who may have died from the disease. Handling sick or dead wild animals should be avoided, as some animals can carry the virus. Healthcare workers and caregivers should use appropriate protective equipment when attending to suspected or confirmed cases. Anyone who has been exposed to a confirmed Ebola case should contact health authorities promptly and follow their instructions on monitoring and other necessary precautions. Vaccines are available against certain types of Ebola virus, but they do not protect against every Ebola virus species. Vaccination programmes and other public health measures depend on the type of virus involved and the circumstances of an outbreak. Ebola Situation in Nigeria As of October 20, 2026, the Federal Government has announced a laboratory-confirmed case of Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). According to the government’s announcement, the patient was a woman who had recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. Following the confirmation, the Federal Government called on public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert. Healthcare workers were urged to maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities. The confirmation of a case does not mean that everyone in Abuja or elsewhere in Nigeria is at risk of infection. Health authorities must assess the patient’s contacts and determine whether anyone had an exposure that could have transmitted the virus. People without a known exposure should remain calm, practise good hygiene and obtain information from official public health announcements rather than relying on rumours or unverified social media reports. Anyone who believes they may have been exposed to the confirmed case should contact the relevant health authorities for guidance. People who develop symptoms after a possible exposure should seek urgent medical advice and notify the healthcare facility before arriving. Difference between ebola and malaria Ebola and malaria can initially produce similar symptoms, particularly fever, headache and weakness. However, the two diseases have different causes and modes of transmission. Ebola is caused by a virus, while malaria is caused by parasites of the genus Plasmodium. Ebola is transmitted primarily through contact with infectious bodily fluids or contaminated materials, whereas malaria is usually transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. Both diseases can cause fever, headache, weakness and vomiting. However, Ebola may cause severe diarrhoea, abdominal pain and bleeding in some patients. Bleeding is not a typical symptom of uncomplicated malaria. The diseases also require different diagnostic tests and treatments. Ebola requires specialised medical care, with specific antibody treatments available for certain types of the disease. Malaria is treated with appropriate antimalarial medicines. Because their symptoms can overlap, it is not possible to reliably distinguish Ebola from malaria based on symptoms alone. Medical assessment and appropriate laboratory testing are necessary to establish the correct diagnosis and ensure that the patient receives the appropriate treatment. items.title: “It’s in God’s hands” – Accident survivor fears she may never find love
items.description: Road accident survivor Grace Akosua Asamoah fears she may never find someone who will love and care for her. She was involved in a terrible accident on March 15, 2024, while travelling from Jukwa to Cape Coast after receiving a distress call from her friend. According to Akosua, six people died on the spot, while several others, including her, sustained critical injuries as a result of the driver’s negligence, alleging that he had fallen asleep at the wheel. The traumatic experience gave her a different perspective on friendships and relationships. During an interview on Joy Prime’s Changes show with host Nikki Samonas , Akosua struggled to answer a question about whether she plans to get married and have children in the future, despite her condition. “Do you have plans of being in a relationship, getting married and having children one day?” Nikki asked “It’s difficult to answer but I can’t say; it’s all in the hands of God. If it pleases God for me to marry, so be it,” she replied. Before the accident, she said she was interested in getting married. However, she has since changed her decision and is now focusing on healing and regaining her facial beauty. Akosua considers the disfigurement of her face one of the reasons she is currently unwilling to pursue a romantic relationship. She is uncertain whether she will find a man who will genuinely love and accept her despite her condition. “Right now getting married and giving birth? No. I wanted to but not now,” When asked whether her condition was one of the reasons for her decision, Akosua responded, “That is one.” Akosua said she prefers to be alone rather than have friends, although she did not disclose the reasons for her preference. However, Nikki encouraged her not to feel inferior or see her condition as a barrier to finding a life partner who would genuinely love and care for her. “Don’t ever think of your position the way you are. There are those in wheelchairs who are married. You’re walking, talking and can eat, cook and work with your hands. The accident didn’t affect your hands, legs and waist. I don’t want you to ever tell yourself that because of this, no man should look at you. I cancel that low self-esteem in Jesus’ name,” Nikki admonished Akosua. Meanwhile, Grace Asamoah is seeking employment, having been at home since the accident. She has been undergoing surgeries to restore her facial appearance but needs financial assistance to cover the cost of the procedures. She is appealing to the public to help her secure a job so she can raise funds for her surgeries. Grace holds a bachelor’s degree in Educational Psychology from the University of Education, Winneba. Although her academic background is in education, she said she is willing to work in any field, citing her knowledge of psychology as an added advantage. She also expressed her willingness to accept support from benevolent individuals who may be willing to sponsor her surgeries or offer them free of charge.

items.title: Siguiri : plus de 20 prévenus condamnés à six mois avec sursis
items.description: ‎Le Tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Siguiri a rendu son verdict, dans une affaire liée à la détention, à la vente et à la consommation de chicha. Sur les prévenus concernés par cette procédure, 21 ont été condamnés à six mois d’emprisonnement avec sursis et au paiement de deux millions de francs guinéens d’amende chacun. Quatre autres ont été relaxés pour infraction non constituée. ‎ ‎Le tribunal a également ordonné la confiscation et l’incinération du produit saisi, identifié sous l’appellation de « Chichara ». ‎ ‎Lors de l’audience du vendredi 16 octobre, le ministère public, représenté par Simon Pierre Millimono, avait requis les mêmes peines contre chacun des prévenus, ainsi que la confiscation et l’incinération des produits saisis. ‎ ‎Cette procédure fait suite à une opération de ratissage menée par les services de sécurité dans plusieurs débits de boissons et boîtes de nuit de Siguiri. Au cours de cette opération, 27 personnes, dont deux mineurs selon les informations communiquées, avaient été interpellées. ‎ ‎À travers cette décision, la justice entend faire respecter les dispositions légales en vigueur. Cette affaire rappelle également l’importance de la prévention et de la sensibilisation pour lutter contre la consommation de substances présentant des risques pour la santé.

items.title: Bamidele mourns Fasoranti, says Nigeria has lost patriot
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA: Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), has described the death of the national leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, at the age of 100 as a great loss to Nigeria, saying the country has lost a patriot par excellence. Bamidele, in a statement he personally signed on Tuesday, described the late elder statesman as a man of uncommon integrity who consistently placed national interest above personal and sectional considerations. The statement read: “I am deeply shocked and saddened by the passing of Pa Reuben Fasoranti, CFR, the foremost leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere. “The late centenarian was a patriot par excellence, a statesman of uncommon integrity who consistently placed national interest far above personal or sectional considerations. “As an educationist, school administrator and community leader, Baba Fasoranti impacted generations of Nigerians and left an indelible mark on our national development trajectory.” The Senate Leader said Fasoranti would be remembered for his principled convictions, selflessness and commitment to true federalism, national unity and progress. He described the deceased as one of the last surviving Awoists and a link between the politics of the First Republic and the Fourth Republic, as well as a custodian of the progressive ideals of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo. “His wise counsel, moral authority and stabilising voice will be sorely missed at this critical period in our national life,” Bamidele said. He extended his condolences, on behalf of his family, constituents and the Senate, to the Fasoranti family, the people of Ondo State, Afenifere and the Yoruba nation. Bamidele prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased and for God to grant his family and associates the strength to bear the loss. items.title: Police forward Obuasi SHTS headmaster Zakaria Abdulai’s case docket to Attorney General
items.description: The police have forwarded the case docket on Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) headmaster Zakaria Abdulai to the Attorney General for study and advice following an investigation into a rape complaint filed by a student. Bekwai Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Lloyd Baidoo, disclosed this on JoyNews’ Top Story on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. He said the Ashanti South Police Command had completed its investigation into the complaint and was awaiting further instructions from the Attorney General. “They have done the investigation, and we have forwarded the case docket to the Attorney General for study and advice. And we, the police, or the Ashanti South Command, are only to patiently wait for further instruction by the Attorney General,” he said. ASP Baidoo said the police would act on any directives issued by the Attorney General. The police spokesperson clarified that the investigation and docket submitted to the Attorney General concern a single complaint filed by a student on August 4, 2026. He said the police could investigate other allegations if additional complainants formally reported them. “In respect of the other matters involving the 19 girls that you are talking about, if they come to police notice, police will subsequently move in and investigate the matter,” he said. The distinction means the case docket currently before the Attorney General relates to the individual complaint investigated by police, rather than all the allegations reported in connection with the school. ASP Baidoo encouraged other students who allege they were abused to lodge official complaints at their nearest police station. “As to the series of cases they are now informing us of, all those parties can just make an official complaint to the nearest police station, and we’ll ensure that we take over and investigate thoroughly,” he said. He also said a report compiled by the Ghana Education Service (GES) committee could be submitted to the police and treated as a complaint to facilitate further investigations. The allegations involving the Obuasi SHTS headmaster have sparked national concern, with at least 19 girls reportedly alleging abuse. The GES has interdicted Mr Abdulai, while the Education Ministry has directed the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) to investigate the allegations. The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has also directed him to step aside from the Juaben Constituency Chairmanship race pending the ongoing process. The submission of the police docket to the Attorney General marks the next stage in the handling of the complaint filed on August 4. Further action by the police will depend on the Attorney General’s advice.

items.title: Des rondes nocturnes pour sécuriser les sites des personnes déplacées
items.description: a Gao, Macina, Bankass et Sevare, les deplaces internes et les refugies font face a des problemes de securite : vols d'equipements, actes de vandalisme et manque de moyens de surveillance. Pour proteger leurs biens et prevenir les incidents, certaines communautes s'organisent en comites de securite et multiplient les rondes nocturnes. Mais ces initiatives locales restent fragiles et les habitants reclament davantage de protection. a Gao, des pompes et des equipements de points d'eau ont ete derobes a Bagoundie 1 et 2, ainsi qu'a la cite Naata, qui accueille des deplaces et des refugies la semaine derniere. Ces vols menacent l'acces a l'eau potable et compliquent le quotidien des residents. Le maire de Gounzoureye, Abdoulkader Younoussa Maïga, appelle la population a contribuer a l'identification des auteurs. Almahamoud Ag Akilini, responsable des sites de deplaces internes dans la region, sollicite quant a lui l'appui des autorites et des personnes de bonne volonte. Macina et Bankass : Des initiatives locales qui ont besoin de soutien a Nemabougou 2, a Macina dans la region de Segou, un vol de mouton a ravive les inquietudes sur un site de deplaces. Souleymane Bouare, l'un des residents, plaide pour des patrouilles regulieres afin de rassurer les habitants et de prevenir d'autres incidents. Toujours au centre du pays, a Bankass, des initiatives portees par des deplaces donnent des resultats. Ils ont cree un comite de securite charge de surveiller le site et de signaler tout comportement suspect. Selon son president, Aly Guindo, aucun vol n'a ete signale depuis sa mise en place. La cohesion entre les residents constitue, selon lui, un atout pour preserver la tranquillite des lieux. A Mopti, le manque d'eclairage impacte les rondes nocturnes a Sevare, les jeunes du site accueillant des deplaces originaires de Tougoumbe organisent des rondes nocturnes pour prevenir les vols et les actes de vandalisme. Cree le 25 fevrier 2025, le comite de securite contribue, selon son president, Amadou Guindo, a maintenir le calme sur le site. Mais les habitants reclament davantage de moyens, notamment l'electricite et l'eclairage, pour renforcer la surveillance durant la nuit. De Gao a Sevare, en passant par Macina et Bankass, pour ces populations deja fragilisees par les deplacements, l'enjeu est de pouvoir vivre dans des conditions plus sûres et dignes. items.title: ISSER advocates enhanced revenue mobilization in 2027 budget
items.description: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) has advised government to use the 2027 national budget to strengthen revenue mobilization and broadened the tax base. ISSER made the call after launching the State of the Ghana Economy Report 2025. According to ISSER, a critical examination of Ghana’s fiscal consolidation in 2025 showed that the economy was driven largely by expenditure restraint rather than increased revenue mobilsation. For example, total grants and revenue amounted to 16.1 percent of GDP while capital expenditure declined from 2.5 percent to 1.4 percent of GDP, raising concerns about public investment. ISSER pointed out that even though the development led to public debt falling to 46 percent from 62.7 percent of GDP reflecting in fiscal adjustment and appreciation of the cedi, the high public expenditure restraint also affected households. Providing some recommendation, the institute said government must strengthen revenue mobilization, broaden the tax base, improve compliance, and reduce revenue leakages. It added that government must enhance productive investment by improving expenditure efficiency while safeguarding priority infrastructure and social spending. Also, ISSER charged government to sustain fiscal discipline by strengthening commitment controls, prevent arrears accumulation, and manage debt refinancing risks. In conclusion under fiscal expenditure, the institute said that Ghana ‘fiscal consolidation was substantial in 2025 but sustaining it will require stronger revenue mobilization in 2027 without sacrificing productive public investment.

items.title: Ikubese mourns Fasoranti, says his gap will be hard to fill
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolutionary Movement, Dr Thomas-Wilson Ikubese, has mourned the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, saying the gap left by the elder statesman would be difficult to fill. In a statement issued on Tuesday night in Akure, Ikubese commiserated with the immediate family of the deceased, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and the people of the state over the loss. He described Fasoranti as a principled advocate of a just society, a disciplinarian and a man who valued order and punctuality. The statement read: “I commiserate with the immediate Fasoranti family, His Excellency Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and the good people of Ondo State on the passing of Pa Reuben Fasoranti a while ago. “The gap he has left behind will be very difficult to fill. “Pa Fasoranti in his lifetime stood up for a just society, even at the expense of his life, as reflected in the assassination attempt on his life orchestrated by the oppressive regime of General Sani Abacha in 1996. “He was also a core disciplinarian who respected time and order.” Ikubese attributed Fasoranti’s longevity, having lived to the age of 100, partly to his disciplined lifestyle, including his eating habits, daily rest and attention to his health. “That he lived up to the ripe age of 100 years was though by the grace of God, but also a reflection of how he compartmentalised his daily activities; not missing out on observing his daily siesta, minding what he eats and listening to his body language, while prioritising his health,” he said. He congratulated Fasoranti’s biological children on inheriting what he described as their father’s good name, saying the many people the late elder statesman touched during his lifetime would be willing to support them. Ikubese prayed that God would grant the deceased’s immediate family, Aiyedatiwa and the people of Ondo State the strength to bear the loss. “It is my prayer that the Lord will grant his immediate family, Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and the good people of Ondo State, the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said. The post Ikubese mourns Fasoranti, says his gap will be hard to fill appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maldives president arrives in Pakistan for three-day visit
items.description: Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday on a three-day visit to Pakistan, according to a statement from his office. Muizzu is visiting Pakistan at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1966. According to the statement, the Maldivian president and first lady were accorded a 21-gun salute upon their arrival at Islamabad International Airport. “The president will be accorded an official welcome tomorrow at Prime Minister House, the official residence of the prime minister of Pakistan,” it added. Later, Muizzu took to X and expressed appreciation for the government and “brotherly people” of Pakistan for their warmth and ceremonial welcome on his first state visit to the country. “I look forward to fruitful engagements that will further deepen our bilateral relations, strengthen our partnership, and advance the shared aspirations of our two nations,” he wrote. An earlier statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) said Muizzu will meet President Asif Ali Zardari, who will host a state banquet in his honour. He will also hold “restricted and delegation-level” talks with PM Shehbaz, the FO said. During the talks, the two leaders will “review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and explore avenues for further strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, health, education, tourism, agriculture, defence, maritime security, climate change and people-to-people exchanges”. They will also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest, according to the FO. A Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum will also be held during the visit to promote interaction between the two countries’ business communities and explore opportunities for trade and investment. “A number of agreements and memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering diverse areas of bilateral cooperation are expected to be signed during the visit,” the statement added. Meanwhile, the Maldivian delegation, led by Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam and comprising cabinet ministers and senior officials, arrived in Islamabad earlier on Tuesday ahead of President Muizzu’s arrival, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement. The delegation was received at the airport by the FO spokesperson, Director General (South Asia and Saarc), the Maldivian high commissioner to Pakistan and the Pakistani high commissioner to the Maldives. In 2015 , former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-premier Nawaz Sharif.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : une voie olympique et des restrictions sur l’autoroute de l’Avenir pour la cérémonie d’ouverture
items.description: À onze jours de la cérémonie d'ouverture des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le Gouverneur de la région de Dakar, Ousmane Kane, a fixé par arrêté, le 20 octobre, les règles de circulation et de stationnement sur l'autoroute de l'Avenir et aux abords du stade Abdoulaye-Wade de Diamniadio. L'événement est prévu le samedi 31 octobre. Une voie olympique de 7 heures à 23 h 30 Sur la section Patte-d'Oie–AIBD de l'autoroute de l'Avenir, la voie de gauche sera réservée à la circulation olympique. De 7 heures à 19 heures, elle sera dédiée aux véhicules circulant de Dakar et de l'AIBD vers le pôle urbain de Diamniadio. De 19 heures à 23 h 30, le sens s'inverse. Sortie n° 11 : accès réservé La sortie n° 11, qui dessert le stade Abdoulaye-Wade, est réservée, de 7 heures à 23 h 30, aux véhicules munis d'un macaron du COJOJ. Dans les périmètres de sécurité des sites de Diamniadio, seuls les véhicules accrédités et les transports collectifs dédiés aux Jeux seront admis. Les spectateurs devront utiliser les navettes ou les cheminements piétonniers aménagés. Où sortir selon d'où l'on vient Les sorties n° 10 et n° 12 resteront ouvertes à la circulation générale pour orienter les spectateurs vers les aires de stationnement et le stade, par des itinéraires balisés. Les spectateurs venant de Dakar pourront emprunter l'une ou l'autre, puis rejoindre le stade par l'autopont de la gare du TER de Diamniadio. Ceux qui arrivent des autres régions sortiront par la sortie n° 12 et suivront la RN2 jusqu'à ce même autopont. Les usagers qui ne se rendent pas à la cérémonie devront emprunter les voies les plus à droite de l'autoroute. Poids lourds : interdiction sur trois axes Les véhicules de transport de marchandises de plus de 3,5 tonnes de poids total autorisé en charge seront interdits de circulation, sauf autorisation pour les livraisons locales. L'interdiction vise l'autoroute à péage entre la Patte-d'Oie et Sébikhotane, dans les deux sens, de 7 heures à 23 h 30. Elle concerne aussi le pont reliant Rufisque à Keur Ndiaye Lô, de 7 heures à 19 heures, et la route nationale n° 1 entre Rufisque et Sébikhotane, de 15 heures à 19 heures. Couloirs de secours maintenus libres L'arrêté impose de garder libres les couloirs de secours aux sorties n° 10, 11 et 12, ainsi que les itinéraires de secours et de dépannage. La SECAA assurera le balisage, la signalisation temporaire et l'information des usagers, en coordination avec le CETUD, le COJOJ, l'AGEROUTE et les forces de défense et de sécurité, également chargés de l'exécution de l'arrêté.

items.title: Appeal court upholds ruling on Zamfara APC primary
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Court of Appeal sitting in Sokoto has dismissed an appeal filed by Senator Sahabi Ya’u Kaura challenging a Federal High Court judgment in Gusau over the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial primary election for Zamfara North. The appellate court upheld the lower court’s decision in favour of Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, an APC senatorial aspirant for Zamfara North, which ordered the conduct of another primary election in the district. Counsel to the first respondent, Bello Galadi, disclosed this while speaking with journalists after the judgment, saying the appellate court resolved all the issues raised by the appellant and dismissed the appeal for lack of merit. Galadi said Kaura had challenged the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court to entertain the suit, but the Court of Appeal upheld the lower court’s authority to hear and determine the matter. He added that the appellate court also rejected the argument that the lower court had improperly shifted the burden of proof to the appellant, noting that the evidence before it established non-compliance with the APC’s rules and guidelines. Describing the judgment as a victory for democracy and the rule of law, Galadi said it reinforced the principle that everyone, regardless of position, was subject to the law. “This judgment has vindicated my client’s decision to pursue the case and sent a strong message to those who consider themselves above the law,” he said. Shinkafi had approached the Federal High Court in Gusau, alleging that the APC senatorial primary election for Zamfara North was not conducted and that there were irregularities in the process. The lower court ruled in his favour and ordered the party to conduct another primary within 14 days. Dissatisfied with the decision, Kaura appealed to the Court of Appeal. Shinkafi welcomed the appellate court’s decision and urged his supporters across Shinkafi, Birnin Magaji, Zurmi and Kaura Namoda local government areas to continue advocating for what he described as equitable political representation. The post Appeal court upholds ruling on Zamfara APC primary appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tambuwal dismisses APC defection rumours
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO: Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he plans to defect from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the claims as false and misleading. The former Sokoto State governor, through his media office, said he had no intention of leaving the ADC, warning that the speculation could create unnecessary confusion ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement dated October 19, 2026, and signed by Prince Daniel, Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to the senator, Tambuwal’s media office reaffirmed his commitment to the ADC and its political objectives. “For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Tambuwal has no plans to join the APC. Suggestions to the contrary are false, baseless and should be disregarded,” the statement said. The clarification comes amid heightened political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 elections, as parties and their leading figures position themselves for the contest. However, the media office insisted that the reports should not be interpreted as an indication of any impending change in Tambuwal’s party affiliation. It explained that the senator’s longstanding relationships with politicians across party lines should not be misconstrued as evidence of a planned defection, noting that his years in public service had enabled him to maintain friendships and political contacts beyond the ADC. The statement also cautioned against drawing conclusions from photographs and video clips circulating on social media, stressing that cordial interactions between politicians from different parties did not necessarily indicate negotiations to change political allegiance. “Political civility is no proof of political realignment,” it said, adding that exchanging greetings or interacting with members of another party should not be presented as evidence of a defection plan. According to the media office, Tambuwal’s immediate priority is to strengthen the ADC, build broader political cooperation and mobilise Nigerians ahead of the next general elections, rather than be distracted by what it described as unsubstantiated claims about his political future. The statement further argued that public discourse should focus on the challenges confronting Nigerians, particularly economic hardship, insecurity and governance concerns, instead of being dominated by rumours about politicians’ movements. “At a time when Nigerians are demanding answers to pressing economic, security and governance challenges, public discussion deserves substance and truth,” the statement said. It urged political stakeholders to concentrate on offering credible leadership and solutions to the country’s problems. The media office also appealed to Tambuwal’s supporters and members of the public to remain focused on the political tasks ahead, while urging media organisations and social media commentators to verify reports concerning the senator’s political affiliation with his office before publication. It reiterated that Tambuwal remained committed to accountable leadership, democratic values and the welfare of Nigerians, insisting that reports linking him to a possible defection to the APC did not reflect his declared political position. The post Tambuwal dismisses APC defection rumours appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Main suspect accused of visa fraud in student's suicide case killed in firing by accomplices: police
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The prime suspect accused of defrauding a 20-year-old student, who allegedly died by suicide, was killed after being shot by his accomplices in Islamabad on Tuesday, claimed police. Laiba Ijaz, a student at International Islamic University, was said to have been defrauded of Rs5 million, which she had paid to move to the United States for further studies. An agent was accused of handing her fake travel documents. The case drew the government’s attention, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directing the police to arrest the suspect. Subsequently, he and two of his female accomplices were later picked up during separate raids in the federal capital. According to the Islamabad police spokesperson, the prime suspect sustained injuries when his accomplices opened fire on cops in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station. The spokesperson said the main suspect has shared information about another suspect, and a police team was taking him to track down the second suspect. It was then that four of the main suspect’s accomplices, who were on two motorcycles, “opened indiscriminate fire on the police party in an attempt get the main suspect freed”, the spokesperson added. The main suspect was injured in the firing while the police team remained safe “due to bulletproof jackets and protective measures”, the spokesperson said. The injured suspect was taken to a hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries, he added. Search operations were underway for arrest of his other accomplices, the spokesperson said. The case A case following Ijaz’s death was registered at the Ramna police station under Sections 322 (unintentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Another separate case was registered by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) on a complaint filed by Ijaz’s maternal uncle under provisions relating to cheating, abetment and immigration-related fraud. According to the FIA, the main suspect had allegedly obtained millions of rupees from Ijaz’s family with the help of a female accomplice and by misrepresenting his identity and professional status. The money was allegedly taken on the pretext of securing employment for her brother and arranging her admission to Harvard University in the US. The suspect was accused of giving Ijaz fake travel documents.

items.title: Élevage : la Haute Autorité du Waqf lance son programme de distribution de chèvres
items.description: La Haute Autorité du Waqf (HAW) et Heifer International Sénégal ont procédé, mardi 20 octobre 2026, à Aéré Lao, dans le département de Podor, à la première remise d’animaux dans le cadre du Waqf agricole public d’élevage de chèvres (WAPEC). Le projet prévoit la distribution progressive de 1 000 chèvres et 100 boucs à 2 000 femmes et jeunes regroupés au sein de 100 groupements dans dix communes des départements de Podor et de Koungheul. Au total, 100 chèvres et 10 boucs ont été remis aux bénéficiaires d’Aéré Lao. Dans le département de Podor, le programme prévoit le placement de 500 chèvres et 50 boucs dans cinq communes : Aéré Lao, Doumga Lao, Gamadji Saré, Guédé Village et Madina Ndiathbè. D’un coût global de 148,4 millions de francs CFA, le WAPEC repose sur le principe du waqf, un mécanisme de solidarité qui vise à préserver et à faire fructifier un bien au bénéfice de la communauté. Ainsi, chaque famille bénéficiaire devra transmettre à une autre famille le même nombre d’animaux reçus, tout en partageant les connaissances acquises. Le dispositif vise à assurer la continuité du projet et à élargir progressivement le nombre de bénéficiaires. « Le waqf, c’est cette aumône qui continue, sadaqah jariyah. On donne une fois, et le bien continue de servir, longtemps après nous », a expliqué le directeur général de la Haute Autorité du Waqf, Dr Ahmed Lamine Athie, invitant les bénéficiaires à prendre soin des animaux pour permettre leur transmission à d’autres familles. Pour sa part, le directeur national de Heifer International Sénégal, Dr Daouda Ndao, a insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer la pérennité de cette chaîne de solidarité. L’organisation est chargée de la mise en œuvre technique du projet, tandis qu’Al Rahma Microfinance accompagnera les groupements dans le financement de leurs activités génératrices de revenus, à travers des mécanismes conformes à la Charia et sans intérêt. La mise en place du programme a été précédée de plusieurs mois de préparation. Dans le département de Podor, les rencontres organisées dans 50 villages ont mobilisé 1 854 personnes, dont 1 684 femmes. Les groupements ont notamment bénéficié de formations en leadership, en gouvernance, en genre et en bonnes pratiques d’élevage. Ils ont également mis en place des systèmes d’épargne et de crédit et commencé des activités de fabrication de savon. La sécurisation du cheptel constitue un autre volet du dispositif. Le lundi 19 octobre, la Compagnie nationale d’assurance agricole du Sénégal (CNAAS) a procédé à l’identification des animaux par des boucles portant chacune un numéro unique, permettant leur traçabilité et leur couverture par une assurance bétail. Cette assurance couvre, pendant un an, les risques de mortalité prévus au contrat. En cas de sinistre couvert, l’éleveur peut percevoir une indemnisation équivalant à 80 % de la valeur assurée de l’animal. Grâce à une subvention de l’État du Sénégal couvrant 50 % de la prime, la contribution de l’éleveur est ramenée de 8 % à 4 % de la valeur de l’animal. Présidant la cérémonie, l’adjoint au préfet du département de Podor, Ousmane Sidibé, a salué une initiative contribuant à la lutte contre la pauvreté, à la solidarité et à la souveraineté alimentaire. Il a souhaité que le programme puisse, à terme, bénéficier à d’autres communes du département. Inscrit dans l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050, le WAPEC entend favoriser l’inclusion économique des femmes et des jeunes en milieu rural, tout en contribuant à la structuration de la filière caprine. La remise des animaux doit se poursuivre dans les autres communes ciblées. Une deuxième cérémonie est prévue jeudi 22 octobre 2026 à Missira Wadène, dans le département de Koungheul.

items.title: OGP : cinq revendications au cœur des attentes du personnel envers la nouvelle direction
items.description: La délégation syndicale de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP) a présenté, ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, ses principales revendications au nouveau directeur général, Mohamed Bangoura, dit « Bank’s », et à son adjoint. La régularisation de 174 recrues, la revalorisation des salaires et la prévention des conflits internes figurent parmi les priorités soulevées. La nouvelle équipe dirigeante de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP) connaît désormais les attentes du personnel. À l’occasion de la cérémonie d’installation des nouveaux responsables, le secrétaire général de la délégation syndicale, Charles Mohamed Kolié, a exposé les principales difficultés auxquelles les travailleurs souhaitent voir apporter des réponses. Au nombre de cinq, les revendications portent essentiellement sur la situation contractuelle des agents, les rémunérations, l’équité dans le traitement du personnel, le renforcement des compétences et l’amélioration du climat social. La régularisation des 174 jeunes recrues de la promotion 2022 constitue l’une des principales préoccupations du syndicat. Selon Charles Mohamed Kolié, ces agents travaillent depuis quatre ans sans disposer d’une situation contractuelle régularisée. La délégation réclame ainsi leur recrutement sous contrat à durée indéterminée (CDI). Elle plaide également pour une revalorisation des salaires des 145 employés permanents en CDI, estimant que leurs rémunérations ne correspondent plus au coût de la vie. La correction des disparités salariales et des inégalités de traitement figure aussi dans le cahier de doléances remis aux nouveaux dirigeants. Le syndicat souhaite, par ailleurs, que des formations professionnelles et des bourses à l’étranger soient accordées aux travailleurs afin de renforcer leurs capacités et de leur permettre de contribuer davantage aux objectifs du Plan stratégique 2030 de l’institution. L’unité de la direction présentée comme un enjeu majeur Au-delà des questions liées aux conditions de travail, la délégation syndicale a insisté sur la nécessité d’une entente entre le directeur général et son adjoint. Pour Charles Mohamed Kolié, la complémentarité de leurs compétences doit servir de levier pour améliorer le fonctionnement de l’OGP. « Soyez un bloc uni, un tandem soudé et sans fissure », a-t-il recommandé aux deux responsables, évoquant les conséquences des divisions internes qui ont marqué l’histoire récente de l’institution. Le syndicat demande également l’instauration d’un mécanisme permanent de dialogue social afin de privilégier le règlement interne des différends et d’éviter de nouvelles crises susceptibles de nuire à l’image de l’Office. Un héritage entre acquis sociaux et tensions Dans son intervention, Charles Mohamed Kolié a tenu à saluer le travail de la direction sortante, en poste pendant un an et dix mois. Il a notamment cité le paiement régulier des salaires, l’apurement des arriérés de 2024, le versement des cotisations à la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS), l’acquisition d’un immeuble de six étages et le renforcement du parc logistique avec des pick-up et des motos. Malgré ces acquis, le responsable syndical a rappelé les difficultés traversées par l’OGP, notamment les procédures judiciaires ayant concerné d’anciens directeurs généraux. « Depuis 2021, deux de nos anciens directeurs généraux ont été limogés et conduits en prison », a-t-il déclaré, appelant les nouveaux responsables à privilégier une gestion fondée sur la transparence, l’équité et la responsabilité. La délégation syndicale affirme être disposée à accompagner la nouvelle équipe dans l’accomplissement de sa mission. Elle attend toutefois des mesures concrètes en faveur du personnel et une gouvernance capable de préserver la stabilité de l’institution. Pour Mohamed Bangoura et son adjoint, ces doléances constituent ainsi les premiers défis sociaux à prendre en compte au début de leur mandat.

items.title: WAFU B U17: Ten-man Black Starlets miss AFCON qualification after 1-0 defeat to Ivory Coast
items.description: Ghana’s under-17 football team, the Black Starlets, have failed to qualify for the 2027 TotalEnergies U-17 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after a painful 1-0 defeat to rivals Côte d’Ivoire. The semi-final clash, played at the ongoing WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship, saw Kassim Ocansey Mingle’s side fall just short of their primary objective despite putting up a spirited performance. The decisive moment of the match arrived when the Ivorians capitalised on their opportunities to break the deadlock. Ghana’s uphill task became even steeper after being reduced to 10 men, forcing the Starlets to play a significant portion of the game at a numerical disadvantage. Despite the setback, Mingle’s boys fought valiantly, creating several half-chances in search of an equalizer. However, the resilient Ivorian defense held firm to book their place in the final and secure one of the coveted AFCON tickets. The result means Ghana’s long wait to return to the continental youth showpiece continues, dealing a heavy blow to the team’s extensive nationwide talent scouting and preparation efforts. Following this exit, the technical team led by Coach Kassim Mingle will turn their attention to regrouping the squad, as the Ghana Football Association (GFA) evaluates its long-term development plans for the country’s youth tiers.

items.title: Governance will suffer if Tinubu campaigns nationwide — Ex-Obidient Chief
items.description: …Challenges critics to debate fuel subsidy removal By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Director-General of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance, also known as the Tinubu Must Stay (TMS) Movement, Marcel Ngogbehei, has said governance could suffer if President Bola Tinubu personally campaigns across all 36 states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient Movement, also challenged critics of the removal of the petrol subsidy to an open debate on the policy, urging them to offer alternatives that take Nigeria’s economic realities into account. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja alongside the National Coordinator of the movement, Engr. Ibrahim Said Uba, during a media parley where he explained why the President might not personally attend campaign activities in every state. “One of the greatest challenges we are having in this country is the time to govern and the time to do electioneering,” Ngogbehei said. He argued that the early commencement of political mobilisation for subsequent elections had undermined governance, with political actors shifting attention away from delivering on their mandates. “A president gets into office, and one year after he gets into office, they start preparing for the next election. And what suffers? Governance suffers,” he said. According to him, Tinubu has chosen to delegate campaign responsibilities to trusted associates to enable him to concentrate on governance. “The President has said, ‘I want to focus on governance. I want to keep an eye on the key things that I am doing. Let the people I have worked with go out there and do the work.’ And in some instances where I need to come in, I will come in. It is pure delegation,” he said. Ngogbehei maintained that effective leadership required building strong teams and institutions rather than depending solely on the physical presence of the leader. “Every good leader must not always be there. If you are a leader that has built resources, that built people, you should trust your people to do the job,” he said. He added: “We don’t want to have a country where you have strong personalities and weak institutions. And that is what we are trying to build for Nigeria.” The TMS director-general urged Nigerians to consider the implications of requiring the President to attend campaign events in every state, arguing that the time devoted to electioneering could come at the expense of governance. “Imagine that the President says, ‘Okay, I am going to be in all the campaigns in thirty-six states of the country.’ What suffers? That is the bottom line. “He can go round the country if he wants to go round, and he has been going round. But let us just understand with him in this particular instance,” he said. Challenges critics to subsidy debate On the removal of the petrol subsidy, Ngogbehei invited critics of the policy to a public discussion on the rationale behind the decision and the alternatives available to the government. He said participants should examine the challenges the policy was intended to address and assess whether alternative approaches could deliver better outcomes. “We are telling the person, let us sit down and let us x-ray these things. “You need to first of all show us that you understand the problem and then, if you were there, what would you do differently, putting into consideration all the complexities of Nigeria?” he asked. Ngogbehei said the invitation was open to individuals and groups, regardless of their political affiliations. “We are open to have this discussion with anyone, anytime, any day. Let us just be open, let us be transparent, let us be factual. It is our country. We cannot run it by propaganda. We cannot run it by lies,” he said. Borrowing would have worsened situation — Uba In his remarks, Uba warned that continued borrowing to sustain the subsidy regime could have exposed the country to more severe fiscal difficulties. He said Nigerians had been warned that maintaining the policy could eventually undermine the government’s ability to meet obligations, including the payment of salaries. Uba described the subsidy removal as a bold decision, while acknowledging that it had imposed short-term hardship on Nigerians. “You might not like him, but he has made a bold and courageous move for the betterment of this country. Do those moves have immediate, short-term impact? Yes,” he said. He urged Nigerians to consider whether the country should bear the economic adjustment costs in the present or leave a potentially heavier burden for future generations. “Is it going to happen in our generation, or does it happen in our children’s generation when it would have been worse?” he asked. Uba said the movement wanted a balanced assessment of the economic situation inherited by the Tinubu administration, the policies introduced and their potential long-term implications. “The Tinubu Must Stay movement is saying, come, let us have a sincere, honest, transparent, and factual analysis of what he met, what he has done, the short-term impact, and what the possible long-term implications are for the country,” he said. The post Governance will suffer if Tinubu campaigns nationwide — Ex-Obidient Chief appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Riziculture en Casamance : le riz « K-Rice Casamance » bientôt disponible sur le marché local
items.description: Avec 2 000 tonnes de semences de riz attendues en 2026, contre un objectif initial de 800 tonnes, KOPIA Sénégal et l’Institut sénégalais de recherches agricoles (Isra) accélèrent la production rizicole en Casamance. Leur défi commun est de transformer cette performance en riz local commercialisé sous la marque « K-Rice Casamance », avec 100 tonnes visées dès 2027 et une montée en puissance du repiquage mécanisé jusqu’à 500 hectares en 2029. ZIGUINCHOR – Dans le sud du pays, la bataille pour l’autosuffisance en riz se joue désormais sur deux fronts. D'abord, il faut produire davantage et mieux vendre le riz local. Le centre KOPIA Sénégal et l’ISRA entendent relever ce défi grâce au projet « K-Rice Casamance », qui associe semences de qualité, mécanisation et commercialisation. Avec des objectifs ambitieux pour les prochaines années, les deux partenaires souhaitent faire de la riziculture un véritable moteur de développement agricole. En 2026, le projet a permis d’aménager 566 hectares de périmètres semenciers dans le bassin de l’Anambé, à Kolda, et dans la région de Ziguinchor, avec 128 producteurs. « Nous misons sur la variété ISRIZ7 pour assurer un approvisionnement régulier en semences de qualité et améliorer les rendements », a expliqué Kim Young Jun, expert du centre KOPIA Sénégal, lors d'une rencontre avec la presse. A lire aussi : Préservation des écosystèmes : 147 hectares de mangrove restaurés pour protéger les communautés côtières Pour accompagner les producteurs, 15 sessions de formation ont été organisées au profit de 721 bénéficiaires, avec un accent sur les techniques de repiquage, l’utilisation des intrants et la lutte contre les maladies et les ravageurs. Au Centre de recherches agricoles de Djibélor, Siméon Bassène, responsable de la production de semences de pré-base, insiste sur la nécessité de moderniser les pratiques. « Le travail manuel ne permettra pas, à lui seul, de cultiver les superficies nécessaires à l’autosuffisance en riz. La mécanisation devient donc indispensable », a-t-il souligné. Grâce aux machines de préparation des pépinières introduites par KOPIA, une semaine suffit désormais pour effectuer des travaux qui prenaient auparavant un mois sur des superficies couvrant les besoins de cinq hectares. La mécanisation pour changer d’échelle Les ambitions du projet se précisent pour les prochaines années. Le repiquage mécanisé, prévu sur 10 hectares en 2027, devra passer à 100 hectares en 2028, puis à 500 hectares en 2029. Des tracteurs, des repiqueuses, des moissonneuses-batteuses et 100 batteuses à riz sont aussi envisagés pour faciliter les opérations et accroître la production. En partenariat avec la coopérative « KABEKEL KUNAARE », qui regroupe 1 151 membres dans les régions de Ziguinchor, Kolda et Sédhiou, le centre KOPIA prépare la mise sur le marché du riz sous la marque « K-Rice Casamance ». Pour 2027, l’objectif annoncé est de commercialiser 100 tonnes de riz, de réaliser un chiffre d’affaires de 70 millions de F Cfa et d’ouvrir trois points de vente. « Nous voulons renforcer la disponibilité de semences de qualité, améliorer les revenus des producteurs et contribuer durablement à l’autosuffisance en riz au Sénégal », a affirmé Kim Young Jun. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: $28bn Lot 2 MoU ‘resurrects’ hope and confidence in Ghana’s Petroleum Hub project
items.description: A US$28-billion agreement signed between the Petroleum Hub Development Corporation (PHDC) and an investment consortium led by Global Sphere of the United Arab Emirates has rekindled optimism across the Ghanaian and broader African energy sectors that the continent’s pursuit of energy security is firmly on course. At a signing ceremony held in Accra on Monday, 19 October 2026, the Chief Executive Officer of the PHDC, Dr Toni Aubynn, and Boubacar Belco Bah, representing a consortium of UAE, Malian and Korean investors, formally executed the Memorandum of Understanding securing Lot 2 of the transformative Petroleum Hub project. According to details disclosed at the well-attended ceremony, the consortium is expected to develop, within five years, a world-class refinery with a capacity of 300,000 barrels per stream day, two petrochemical plants, four million cubic metres of storage infrastructure, and a multi-berth jetty. Implementation is scheduled to commence immediately with on-site activities at the project location in Jomoro expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with strong anticipation that the agreement will deliver substantial and lasting transformative benefits. In his address, the Minister of Energy and Green Transition, Hon. Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, mentioned that the Petroleum Hub project is indispensable to President John Dramani Mahama’s vision for Ghana’s energy sector, noting that, with Ghana recording significant advances in the upstream sector of its oil and gas industry, it has become imperative to establish infrastructure linking the upstream and downstream sectors and the Petroleum Hub, he affirmed, provides the ideal solution. The Minister reiterated that his Ministry will extend full support to the PHDC and the investors in the development of Lot 2. “Government has been working tirelessly to develop this sector. The President’s vision is clear: we cannot increase oil production without adding value to our resources. That is why the Petroleum Hub constitutes a pivotal element of the entire petroleum value chain. “We have collaborated closely with Dr Toni Aubynn and his team to realise this ambition. I am delighted that today we are securing investors and partners through this US$28-billion agreement. Today’s signing ceremony is not the culmination of the process; it is the beginning,” he stated. Boubacar Belco Bah, speaking on behalf of the consortium, affirmed the group’s strong commitment to fulfilling the terms of the agreement and advancing construction of the project. He emphasised that the consortium would continue to work closely with the PHDC to ensure strict adherence to the timelines set out in the agreement. “Ultimately, our success will be measured not by the agreement we sign today, but by the commitments we honour and the results we achieve together. “We are committed to collaborating closely with the PHDC, AMS Technologies, the Project Development Consortium, and qualified technical and financial institutions to advance a project that is technically credible, commercially sustainable, and financially bankable. “Our approach will prioritise rigorous project preparation, responsible risk allocation, transparent governance, and effective stakeholder coordination. We also intend to combine international expertise with meaningful participation by Ghanaian contractors, professionals, and service providers,” he said. On his part, the Chief Executive Officer of the PHDC, Dr Toni Aubynn, described the MoU as a major milestone for the Corporation, made possible only through the unwavering support of His Excellency President John Dramani Mahama and the sector Minister, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor. He highlighted the project’s central role in Ghana’s economic and energy transformation and assured stakeholders that the PHDC, under his leadership, would ensure effective implementation of the agreement. “To our investors, welcome. You have made a significant commitment, and we recognise the confidence that commitment represents. The Petroleum Hub Development Corporation will provide the necessary support systems to help translate this partnership into a successful project. “And to the management and staff of the Petroleum Hub Development Corporation, I wish to speak directly to you. “We have come a long way since 18 March 2025. We have navigated uncertainty, undertaken engagements at various levels, and laid the foundations for the progress we celebrate today. “Yet the signing of this agreement is not the end of our work. It is the beginning of a new chapter of responsibility. The true measure of our success will be the infrastructure we build, the investments we deliver, the jobs we create, and the lasting value we leave for the people of Ghana,” he concluded. Among those present at the ceremony were the Deputy Minister for Energy, Richard Gyan-Mensah; the Deputy Minister for Transport, Dorcas Afo Toffey; the President of the Western Regional House of Chiefs, Nana Kobina Nketsia; the Paramount Chief of the Western Nzema Traditional Area, Awulae Kwasi Armahchi III; the Member of Parliament for Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira, Kofi Nokoe; and a host of high-level delegates

items.title: Rotary Club of Accra-Airport launches “Arise for Polio 2026’
items.description: The Rotary Club of Accra-Airport, has launched ARISE FOR POLIO 2026 , an initiative to help ensure that no child, anywhere in the world, suffers from polio again. Speaking at the launch, the President of Rotary Club of Accra-Airport, Rotarian David Kwatia Nyante, said, Polio is a devastating disease that can cause permanent paralysis and even death. Yet, it is preventable through vaccination. When Rotary launched its PolioPlus programme in 1985, hundreds of thousands of children were being paralyzed by polio every year. Today, through the collective efforts of Rotary, governments, health workers and international partners, wild poliovirus remains endemic in only two countries — Afghanistan and Pakistan. “That is remarkable progress, but our work is not finished. Until polio is eradicated everywhere, children everywhere remain at risk. For over four decades, Rotarians have remained committed to this cause, contributing their time, resources and energy to support immunization programmes and raise awareness. Here in Ghana, Rotary continues to work with the Ghana Health Service and other partners to protect children. The Rotary Club of Accra-Airport is proud to be part of this global effort.” Rotarian David Nyante explained. He added that, no single organisation can achieve this goal alone. “We need governments, businesses, communities and individuals to play their part. That is the spirit behind Arise for Polio. We have come together to raise awareness and to mobilise support and strengthen partnerships that will help us finish the job. To our corporate partners and prospective sponsors, supporting this cause is an investment in children’s health, stronger communities and a better future. It is also an opportunity to be part of something truly historic.” The District Governor, Rotary International District 9104, Rotarian Jack Andrews Dotsey (PhD), who was the keynote speaker, commended the Rotary Club of Accra-Airport for organizing this event and, more importantly, for reminding us that although tremendous progress has been made against polio, our responsibility is not over. Speaking on the theme: “Together, We Finish the Fight”, Rotarian Dotsey said, for decades, Rotary has worked alongside governments, communities and international partners to protect children from polio. This commitment goes beyond fundraising. Rotarians advocate, Rotarians mobilise communities, and Rotarians support vaccination campaigns. Rotarians work with health professionals. And, Rotarians help build trust so that vaccines can reach children wherever they live. “The progress achieved demonstrates what sustained leadership, partnership and service can accomplish. But with polio, being almost successful is not enough. As long as the poliovirus continues to circulate anywhere, children everywhere remain potentially at risk. That is why our message today is simple: “We must finish what we started,” he concluded. The chair of Ghana National PolioPlus, Rotarian Gertrude Adzo Akpalu, Past Assistant Governor of Rotary International District 9104, speaking to the media at the event said, “We are at 99.9% on Polio eradication with the Wild Polio Virus endemic only in Afghanistan & Pakistan. Our 2026 theme is One day. One focus: ending Polio for good. Rotary in collaboration with GHS/EPI, WHO, UNICEF, Gates Foundation, Gavi, US-CDC, Pediatric Society of Ghana, Civil Society, Polio Survivors and the Media must make history by ending Polio. Let it be our legacy – let us donate to the Rotary Foundation PolioPlus Fund, share info and continue to create awareness (be advocates) and learn by taking action! Polio anywhere is Polio everywhere! Together, we must end Polio!”

items.title: NAZA: When technology makes killing a calculation
items.description: GOA, India – There are films that recount the horrors of war, films that make audiences feel the pain of those who endure it, and films that take us somewhere far more disturbing: into the machinery that makes such horrors possible. NAZA, the documentary by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, belongs to this third category. It asks us to look beyond the images of destruction that have become tragically familiar from Gaza and confront the systems, institutional cultures and technological processes through which the destruction of human life can be organised, assessed and justified.
