items.title: Festival de Marrakech 2026 : Kleber Mendonça Filho parrain des 9es Ateliers de l’Atlas
items.description: La 9e édition des Ateliers de l’Atlas se tiendra du 22 au 26 novembre 2026, en marge du Festival International du Film de Marrakech, prévu du 20 au 28 novembre. Cette année, 30 projets et films issus de 14 pays ont été retenus parmi 410 candidatures. Le cinéaste brésilien Kleber Mendonça Filho, récompensé à Cannes pour L’Agent secret, sera le parrain de cette édition dédiée au développement des cinémas marocain, arabe et africain. Les Ateliers de l’Atlas dévoilent leur sélection pour leur 9e édition. Organisée dans le cadre du Festival International du Film de Marrakech, cette plateforme professionnelle consacrée à l’accompagnement des cinéastes marocains, arabes et africains réunira, du 22 au 26 novembre 2026, des réalisateurs émergents et confirmés autour de projets à différents stades de leur production. Pour cette édition, 30 projets et films provenant de 14 pays ont été sélectionnés parmi 410 candidatures. Cette sélection comprend 14 projets en développement, 11 films en tournage ou en postproduction et cinq projets marocains réunis dans la section « Regards sur l’Atlas ». Le programme sera placé sous le parrainage du réalisateur brésilien Kleber Mendonça Filho, figure majeure du cinéma contemporain, dont le parcours témoigne d’un engagement en faveur d’un cinéma indépendant et audacieux. Kleber Mendonça Filho, un parrain de premier plan Réalisateur et scénariste reconnu sur la scène internationale, Kleber Mendonça Filho s’est notamment illustré avec Les Bruits de Recife (2012), Aquarius (2016) et Bacurau (2019), qui a remporté le Prix du Jury au Festival de Cannes. Son dernier film, L’Agent secret, a été récompensé par le Prix de la mise en scène à Cannes en 2025, avant de recevoir deux Golden Globes et quatre nominations aux Oscars en 2026, selon les informations communiquées par le festival. Le cinéaste voit dans son rôle de parrain une occasion de découvrir de nouvelles générations de créateurs et de nourrir sa propre réflexion artistique. « Être à l’écoute d’idées nouvelles et saisir les aspirations des nouvelles générations de cinéastes est une source d’inspiration pour mon propre travail » , a-t-il déclaré, évoquant également son attachement à Marrakech et au festival. Il estime que cette expérience lui donnera le sentiment d’assister à la naissance de nouveaux films. Trente projets et films issus de 14 pays La sélection réunit des œuvres venues d’Algérie, du Cap-Vert, d’Égypte, d’Éthiopie, de Jordanie, du Liban, de Libye, du Maroc, de Palestine, du Rwanda, du Sénégal, du Soudan, de Syrie et de Tunisie. Les 14 projets en développement comprennent 12 fictions et deux documentaires, dont six premiers longs métrages. Plusieurs réalisateurs déjà remarqués sur la scène internationale figurent parmi les participants, notamment Amjad Abu Alala, connu pour You Will Die at Twenty, Laila Abbas, réalisatrice de Thank You for Banking With Us, Meryem Benm’Barek, à qui l’on doit Sofia et Derrière les palmiers, ainsi que Sofia Alaoui (Animalia) et Yasmine Benkiran (Reines). La catégorie des films en tournage ou en postproduction compte 11 œuvres, dont cinq premiers longs métrages. Quatre d’entre elles avaient déjà bénéficié du soutien des Ateliers de l’Atlas lors de leur développement : Seasons of the Weary Kind de Samuel Ishimwe, Eldorado d’Alaa Eddine Aljem, Fagadaga de Yoro Mbaye et Wolfmother d’Ismaël El Iraki. Le retour de ces films à un stade plus avancé de leur production illustre la continuité de l’accompagnement proposé par la plateforme, depuis les premières étapes d’un projet jusqu’à sa concrétisation. La section « Regards sur l’Atlas » mettra, quant à elle, en lumière cinq projets marocains, dont quatre fictions et un documentaire. À travers des récits intimes, des bouleversements politiques et des explorations de la mémoire collective, les œuvres sélectionnées reflètent la diversité des écritures et des réalités qui traversent les sociétés contemporaines. Atlas Station accompagne la nouvelle génération marocaine En parallèle de cette sélection, Atlas Station poursuivra son travail d’accompagnement des jeunes professionnels du cinéma marocain. Le programme accueillera huit producteurs, quatre femmes et quatre hommes, choisis parmi 30 candidatures. Ils bénéficieront d’un parcours de perfectionnement consacré aux différentes dimensions de la production cinématographique, grâce à des rencontres et à des échanges avec des professionnels internationaux. Atlas Station soutiendra également cinq courts métrages marocains en postproduction, retenus parmi 24 candidatures. Cette sélection comprend quatre fictions et un documentaire. Les films bénéficieront d’un accompagnement adapté à leurs besoins, notamment pour leur finalisation et leur diffusion. Atlas Programs, un dispositif élargi pour soutenir le cinéma Créés en 2018, les Ateliers de l’Atlas s’inscrivent désormais dans Atlas Programs, un ensemble d’initiatives professionnelles porté par le Festival International du Film de Marrakech. Aux côtés des Ateliers de l’Atlas et d’Atlas Station, Atlas Press accompagne le développement de la critique cinématographique. Atlas Distribution Meetings favorise, pour sa part, les échanges entre une soixantaine de professionnels venus d’Afrique, du monde arabe et d’Europe afin de faciliter la circulation des films. Le dispositif comprend également Atlas Distribution Awards, destiné à soutenir la distribution des œuvres. Les Ateliers de l’Atlas, Atlas Station et Atlas Distribution Meetings se dérouleront à Marrakech du 22 au 26 novembre 2026. Atlas Press est programmé du 23 au 27 novembre. Avec cette nouvelle édition, le Festival International du Film de Marrakech confirme ainsi sa volonté de renforcer l’accompagnement des talents et de favoriser l’émergence de nouvelles œuvres issues des cinémas marocain, arabe et africain, tout en encourageant les collaborations professionnelles à l’échelle internationale. The post Festival de Marrakech 2026 : Kleber Mendonça Filho parrain des 9es Ateliers de l’Atlas appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: NECA, SON reject proposed NAFDAC bill, warn of regulatory duplication
items.description: By Soni Daniel Employers’ body urges National Assembly to exclude tobacco products from legislation The Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA), the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) and industry operators have rejected aspects of the proposed Food, Medical Products and Related Products (Registration, Etc.) Bill, 2026, warning that the legislation could create regulatory conflicts, duplicate existing laws and disrupt legitimate businesses. NECA, in a formal submission to the Senate Committee on Health, urged the National Assembly to exclude tobacco products from the proposed legislation, arguing that the sector is already subject to a dedicated regulatory framework. The Bill, sponsored by Senator Umar Sadiq Suleiman, passed second reading in the Senate on July 21, 2026. It seeks to repeal the Food, Drugs and Related Products Act, 2004, and establish a new regulatory framework for food, medical and related products. However, NECA argued that extending the Bill’s provisions to tobacco products could conflict with the National Tobacco Control Act, 2015, the National Tobacco Control Regulations, 2019, and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria Act, 2015. According to the employers’ association, the proposed framework could create overlapping responsibilities among the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, SON and the Nigeria Customs Service. It warned that such overlaps could lead to multiple product-registration requirements, duplicated approvals, conflicting enforcement decisions, increased compliance costs and uncertainty for businesses. NECA maintained that tobacco products constitute a distinct regulatory category and should not be treated as food or medicines under the proposed law. It also argued that NAFDAC’s existing statutory mandate does not expressly cover tobacco products, adding that their inclusion in the Bill could extend the agency’s authority into an area already governed by dedicated legislation. The association further raised concerns about provisions granting additional powers over product registration, suspension, seizure, factory operations and enforcement, warning that these could conflict with the responsibilities of existing regulatory institutions. Of particular concern to NECA is the proposed ceiling-list mechanism, which it said could give NAFDAC excessive administrative discretion to restrict products without adequate statutory safeguards and oversight. The association called on lawmakers to introduce safeguards against unilateral regulatory decisions, strengthen coordination among existing institutions and amend the Bill to prevent duplication, regulatory uncertainty and unnecessary disruption to businesses. It stressed that a coherent regulatory environment was essential for investment, economic growth, effective public-health protection and compliance with the law. NECA also urged lawmakers to ensure that the proposed legislation complemented, rather than contradicted, Nigeria’s existing tobacco-control framework. The association said effective regulation should be based on clearly defined institutional responsibilities, predictable compliance requirements, proportionate enforcement and coordination among relevant government agencies. It expressed readiness to engage further with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to achieve a legislative outcome that protects public health while sustaining regulatory certainty and business confidence. Health Ministry, SON seek deferment The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare also expressed reservations about the proposed amendments at a public hearing on the Bill. Represented by Dr Adebisi Adegoke, mni, Director of Hospital Services, the Ministry raised concerns about potential regulatory conflicts, duplication and overlapping mandates, which it said could undermine effective government administration. It recommended deferring consideration of the Bill to allow further consultations among affected stakeholders and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s existing responsibilities. SON similarly raised concerns that some provisions of the proposed legislation conflicted with the law establishing the organisation and could interfere with its statutory responsibilities. The standards body backed the call for the Bill’s consideration to be deferred, arguing that a more comprehensive review was needed to remove unnecessary complexities and overlapping mandates. It also expressed concern that the process leading to the proposed amendments had not involved sufficient engagement and consultation with affected institutions. Industry operators warn of business disruption Tobacco industry operators have also expressed reservations about the proposed legislation, warning that another layer of regulation could complicate compliance rather than improve regulatory effectiveness. At a recent public hearing, industry stakeholders argued that tobacco manufacturing, importation, distribution, packaging, health warnings, product standards and related activities were already subject to extensive statutory controls. They warned that parallel approval and enforcement structures could expose manufacturers and importers to conflicting directives, additional administrative costs, operational disruptions and uncertainty over which regulator has final authority. The operators maintained that their concerns were not about resisting public-health regulation but about the risks of multiplying regulatory requirements without clearly demonstrated public-policy benefits. They further argued that unpredictable compliance obligations could weaken investor confidence, discourage business expansion and complicate efforts by the Federal Government to improve Nigeria’s competitiveness and ease of doing business. According to the industry position, unnecessary administrative burdens on compliant businesses could also divert regulatory attention and resources from more pressing enforcement challenges, including illicit trade and non-compliant operators. items.title: Puits Goumeri W-8 : l’expertise algérienne de la Sonatrach achève sa mission d’appui au Niger…
items.description: Les experts algériens dépêchés par la Sonatrach ont achevé leur mission au Niger, après avoir apporté leur appui technique dans la gestion de l’incident survenu aux puits Goumeri W-8, dans le bloc pétrolier d’Agadem. Leur intervention s’inscrit dans le cadre de la solidarité et de la coopération entre les deux pays dans le secteur des hydrocarbures. Dépêchée à la suite d’une décision du président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune, la délégation de la Sonatrach a partagé son savoir-faire avec les équipes nigériennes mobilisées pour maîtriser l’éruption de pétrole et de gaz constatée sur les puits Goumeri W-8. Les experts ont contribué à l’analyse des circonstances de l’incident, à l’évaluation des dégâts techniques et environnementaux ainsi qu’à l’identification de solutions appropriées. L’incident, survenu le 25 septembre 2026, a été caractérisé par des projections de pétrole brut et de gaz à plus de dix mètres de hauteur, selon les autorités nigériennes. Le 14 octobre 2026, la délégation algérienne s’est rendue sur le site d’Agadem aux côtés des autorités nigériennes. La mission de terrain, conduite avec les ministres du Pétrole et de l’Environnement, a permis d’évaluer la situation, de superviser les opérations de sécurisation de la plateforme et de suivre les mesures destinées à limiter l’écoulement de brut et les impacts environnementaux. À l’issue de ce séjour, les experts ont soumis leur rapport final aux ministères nigériens du Pétrole et de l’Environnement au cours du week-end. Ce document est appelé à éclairer les autorités sur les constats techniques, les risques résiduels et les recommandations pour la reprise durable du contrôle des puits. Pour marquer la fin de la mission, les experts algériens ont été reçus cet après-midi en audience par le président de la République, le général d’armée Abdourahamane Tiani. La rencontre s’est déroulée en présence des ministres sectoriels en charge du dossier, M. Hamadou Tinni, ministre du Pétrole, et le colonel Abdoulaye Maizama, ministre de l’Environnement. Cette audience traduit l’importance accordée par les plus hautes autorités nigériennes à la gestion de l’incident et à la coopération technique avec l’Algérie. Elle illustre également le rôle croissant de la Sonatrach comme partenaire d’expertise dans la maîtrise des défis liés à l’exploitation pétrolière au Sahara. items.title: All the President’s Hotties
items.description: “T here are some reasons to be president,” Donald Trump mused at a rally in Georgia earlier this month. Take a wild guess what these might be. The cool armored car? Custody of the nuclear button? The opportunities for immense corruption? Wrong. The leader of the free world was referring to the joy of living in a house guarded by “big, strong, handsome soldiers.” Under Joe Biden, soldiers were not allowed to be hot, because of woke. Even worse, some of them were girls . Yes, after two grinding years of governance, Trump is back in his happy place, out on the campaign trail, voicing whichever disconnected thoughts crackle and fizz through his frontal cortex. His favorite rhetorical theme lately is an unexpected one: the official presidential dreamboat rankings. In multiple rallies, Trump has gone on and on about the relative hotness of male politicians, soldiers, and even protesters. As a result, people on the internet have diagnosed him with a novel medical condition: gay dementia . After putting in a solid shift in the heterosexuality mines, has the former beauty-pageant proprietor now become so disinhibited that he can no longer repress his thirst for man-flesh? A less salacious explanation might be that the president has always refined his speeches based on audience feedback, and he’s discovered that his hot-guy material absolutely kills. In 2024, he kept going on about “the late, great Hannibal Lecter” and whether being electrocuted is preferable to being eaten by a shark, simply because the crowds enjoyed those riffs. Today the MAGA faithful get a transgressive thrill from hearing a man put into office by Christian conservatives deliver homoerotic stylings on male beauty. Calling women hot would read as creepy, and might remind audiences of the sexual-assault allegations against Trump, or the locker-room gaucheness of “grab ’em by the pussy.” But lusting after men is good, clean fun, and after a decade pushing the limits of outrageous behavior, here is a taboo that Trump can harmlessly break. Which Democrat is going to mock a guy for being a little bit swishy? Stephen Miller will not dare whisper to his boss: Sir, you know that we keep snidely implying that James Talarico is secretly gay? Your obvious love of buff soldiers is giving—mixed messages. E nough of the serious chin-stroking electoral analysis, though. You want to hear which men America’s greatest president considers to be stone-cold babes. Step forward, Jon Husted of Ohio, with your glorious, rippling glutes and your valiant crusade against energy-efficient dishwashers. At a campaign stop for the Republican Senate nominee in Dayton, Trump discovered that Husted used to be a star football player. Naturally, the president looked for evidence of this in Husted’s buttocks—the windows to the soul. As he later told a crowd in Youngstown: “I don’t do this with men very often.” (A lie.) “I started examining his body because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass.” The crowd laughed, which encouraged Trump to add that he also admired Husted’s hands, which he said were “like claws.” [ Read: The king of queens ] Days later in Kentucky, Trump returned to the theme of Husted’s badonkadonk. “I examined his ass, and then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline,” he told the crowd. “I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering.” The Ohio candidate had gained “nine or 10 points since I talked about that,” he said. (Also a lie.) Trump has always had a weakness for a photogenic guy. He reportedly chose members of his Cabinet, such as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, after seeing how good they looked on television. He’s long made a habit of singling out attractive men in his audiences, entreating the rest of the crowd to join in his appreciation. (“Get up here, please. I want to see,” he told a muscled young man at a Coast Guard ceremony this spring.) Back in February, the president described a “very powerful” steel-factory owner who was so grateful for his policies that “he said, ‘Sir, I want to kiss you so badly.’” In May, my colleague Ashley Parker chronicled some of the men whose looks had Trump favorably assessed. These included the president of Paraguay (“young and handsome”), military pilots (“perfect specimens”), and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (“under that beautiful exterior is a killer”). The president’s homoerotic stylings have become more obvious, however, because he has so little else to talk about on the campaign trail. Crooked Hillary and Sleepy Joe have long since departed the scene, Shifty Schiff’s impeachment plans went nowhere, and the fake-news media have been replaced by MAGA toadies. With few enemies left (except his own terrible judgment) Trump is struggling to develop new material. Like many older people, he has retreated to his comfort zone, and his comfort zone is guarded by big, strapping men in uniform. “They’re always great-looking, these four-star guys. I don’t know if they get the job by their look,” he told a rally in Kansas this week . He also praised the rock singer Ted Nugent for having a son who was “a beautiful-looking guy.” The president has ruminated so often on male beauty lately that it’s become very obvious that he has a type. His taste in men turns out to be somewhat basic—white, beefy, butch; think corn-fed midwestern fireman—and thoroughly partisan. At the same rally in Georgia where he enthused about the White House guards, Trump incorrectly declared that Senator Jon Ossoff, a Democrat, was not a “good-looking man,” unlike his Republican challenger. “I actually think Mike Collins is a good-looking man—and he’s all man. He’s all man,” added Trump. “I’m not sure about Ossoff.” (Let me save you a click: Collins is a mulleted 59-year-old with a touch of latter-day Newt Gingrich about his facial features, whereas Ossoff is so cute that he clearly had to shave off his beard in order to be taken seriously.) Trump went on to declare that the GOP candidate for Georgia governor, Rick Jackson, was also a “very handsome, distinguished, beautiful-looking guy.” In Kansas, Trump expanded his hotness rankings to encompass the crowd. Describing one loyalist’s confrontation with a protester, he noted approvingly that “the MAGA guy beat the crap out of him. Not that that matters. Good-looking guy.” Trump’s MAGA goggles do have some limits. Last month, he went through a phase of roasting Ken Paxton, devoting sections of multiple speeches to what a schlub he found the Republican Senate candidate in Texas to be. “He may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen,” the president observed on September 9, adding the next day: “I’m not sure if I like your look. I’m not sure if I like the way you dress. I don’t like the way you talk.” Sad! Paxton, apparently, has a face not even a homoerotically inclined Republican president can love. A n enthusiasm for buff young men in uniforms (or out of them) has always been one of the hallmarks of authoritarianism—a form of governance enamored of strong male bodies, and the promise of violence that they contain, even when the rulers consider overt homosexuality degenerate. Mussolini’s Italy simultaneously exiled dozens of gay men to the island of San Domino and produced the jaw-droppingly campy naked statues at the Stadio dei Marmi in Rome. Many dictators end up mired in camp: Muammar Qaddafi had an all-female bodyguard troop. Turkmenistan’s Saparmurat Niyazov renamed April after his mother and built a gold statue of himself that rotated to face the sun. Emperor Bokassa I of the short-lived Central African empire tried to make his coronation ceremony an exact replica of the one held by Napoleon Bonaparte, but was hampered by having to hold it in a basketball stadium. [ Read: The surprising reason for the new homophobia ] Donald Trump’s simultaneous love for unchecked executive power and a well-turned male ankle is therefore part of a rich historical tradition. At the same time, it is also one of the many ways in which his political style represents a departure from typical American conservatism. From the 1970s onward, the Republicans were the party of the “moral majority” and “traditional values.” The idea that the party’s base is casually homophobic is still such conventional wisdom that J. D. Vance, a Millennial who very obviously had LGBTQ friends in his student years, now has to play-act as an old-school social conservative to show the depth of his political conversion. When a man at a rally in Texas shouted out that he loved Vance, the vice president replied : “I love you too, sir. In a totally platonic way, to be clear. I’m the vice president, not James Talarico.” Vance does not seem to have grasped that his boss’s campiness is key to his political appeal—it’s the secret sauce that transforms nastiness into showbiz sass. Trump is politics’ answer to Joan Rivers, and his persona is influenced by all the flavors of American fakery: the carnival barker, the reality-TV host, the kayfabe world of professional wrestling. He looks like a man doing a drag performance as himself. Trump’s embrace of camp also reflects his immunity to shame. I get the sense that Vance is crippled with embarrassment by the thought of that famous picture of him in eyeliner and a blond wig. His unease with gayness, campiness, and femininity reads as insecurity. By contrast, Trump loves Sunset Boulevard and doesn’t care who knows it. Hell, he even went to Liza Minnelli’s wedding. That authenticity and disinhibition means he can get a crowd of white Christians in Kentucky to listen to his homoerotic ramblings—and applaud.

items.title: A state that can’t contain galamsey, now turning full aggression on ‘hate speech’? – Yaw Nsarkoh
items.description: Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the state’s approach to alleged speech offences, arguing that the apparent urgency in pursuing people over social media posts contrasts with its continued struggle to contain illegal mining. He challenged the authorities to justify the use of state power against individuals over online expressions while galamsey continues to threaten water bodies, forest reserves and livelihoods across the country. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, Mr Nsarkoh criticised what he described as the state’s misplaced priorities in addressing the country’s pressing governance challenges. He said the authorities appeared unable to stop illegal mining but were willing to direct significant attention towards people who make controversial comments on social media. “But what is happening when the state which cannot contain illegal miners, Galamsey, now turns its full aggression on people who make one impolitic post on Facebook?” he asked. Mr Nsarkoh also expressed concern about what he described as the loose application of serious criminal charges in response to public comments. “How can we rationalise these sometimes very loose uses of serious charges like treason?” he questioned. His comments formed part of a broader critique of Ghana’s governance system, which he said appeared unable to address major threats to the country while becoming increasingly aggressive towards certain forms of public expression. Mr Nsarkoh acknowledged the need for discipline in society and said reckless defamatory statements should be discouraged. However, he argued that such efforts must not undermine legitimate criticism or distract the state from more pressing national challenges. “I am all for discipline in society and the discouragement of reckless defamatory talk. Democracy is not the same as disorder,” he said. He warned that citizens’ legitimate concerns risk being ignored when the state focuses on punishing controversial expressions while failing to address problems such as illegal mining. The former corporate executive further cautioned against a situation in which people become afraid to criticise those in authority, arguing that institutions that do not accommodate feedback and critical scrutiny risk stagnation. Mr Nsarkoh’s remarks come amid wider national debates over the limits of freedom of expression, the handling of alleged offensive or unlawful speech, and the state’s response to illegal mining. He urged a governance approach that balances lawful accountability with the protection of legitimate criticism and a stronger commitment to addressing the country’s persistent environmental and social challenges.

items.title: Uduaghan’s remains arrive in Warri, as Oborevwori visits family
items.description: Obi, Ebie, Obaseki, Iyovwaye pay tributes to former Delta governor By Jimitota Onoyume WARRI — The remains of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, arrived in the state on Tuesday, as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and his wife, Deaconess Tobore Oborevwori, joined members of the deceased’s family to receive them at Osubi Airport in Okpe Local Government Area. Oborevwori and his wife later visited the family at the former governor’s residence in Warri to commiserate with his wife, Deaconess Roli Uduaghan, and other relatives. Speaking during the visit, the governor described the late Uduaghan as his boss, recalling the political support he received from the former governor, who appointed him as one of his special advisers in 2007. “He contributed immensely to the development of Delta State, most especially the Asaba International Airport. He was a man of few words. He was very articulate, calm. He has gone, but he can never be forgotten by Deltans,” Oborevwori said. Uduaghan’s death was announced on Monday by his son, Toju. According to the announcement, the former governor died at the age of 71. He governed Delta State from 2007 to 2015 and also served as commissioner for health and secretary to the state government during the administration of former Governor James Ibori. Meanwhile, tributes have continued to pour in from political leaders and public figures, including the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi; Chairman of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Mr Chiedu Ebie; former Edo State Governor, Godwin Obaseki; and NDC governorship candidate in Delta State, Deacon Chris Iyovwaye. Uduaghan treated me like a younger brother — Obi Obi said he was deeply saddened by Uduaghan’s death, recalling the cordial relationship they shared while serving as governors of Anambra and Delta states, respectively. In a condolence message, the former Anambra governor said Uduaghan treated him like a younger brother and that they worked together on issues of national development. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my very dear elder brother, His Excellency, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State. In my interactions with him, he treated me like his junior brother,” Obi said. He recalled their collaboration in advocating for the award of the contract for the Second Niger Bridge, which he described as important to national integration, commerce and the development of the South-East and South-South. “I recall with fondness the cordial working relationship I enjoyed with him during our time in public service. We worked together as brothers in the collective effort to promote and advocate for the award of the contract for the Second Niger Bridge, recognising its importance to national integration, commerce, and the development of the South-East and South-South. “I am pleased that the effort ultimately succeeded and that the Second Niger Bridge became a reality, serving as a symbol of the importance of collaboration in the pursuit of national development,” he said. Obi extended his condolences to Uduaghan’s family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state, praying for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul. His contributions will inspire future generations — Ebie Ebie described Uduaghan’s death as a moment of collective grief, saying the former governor’s contributions to public service and the development of Delta State would continue to inspire future generations. In a statement issued by his media aide, Jerome-Mario Utomi, the NDDC chairman said Uduaghan’s life was closely connected to the aspirations and development of his people. “Beyond the offices he occupied and the political milestones he recorded, Dr Uduaghan was a son of Delta whose life was intertwined with the aspirations, challenges and development journeys of his people. His passing is not merely a family tragedy; it is a moment of collective grief for all who valued his contributions to public life,” Ebie said. He added that the former governor’s legacy should be measured by the lives he touched, the responsibilities he discharged and his contributions to society. On behalf of his family, members of the NDDC Governing Board and management, Ebie extended condolences to the Uduaghan family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state. He prayed God to grant the family the strength to bear the loss and the deceased eternal rest. Uduaghan brought deep sense of service to public life — Obaseki Obaseki also expressed sadness over Uduaghan’s death, describing it as a loss to his family, Delta State, the South-South region and Nigeria’s political community. The former Edo governor said Uduaghan, a medical doctor by training, brought a strong sense of service to public office and contributed to the development of Delta State during his eight years as governor. “His death is a painful loss, not only to his family and the people of Delta State, but to the South-South region and the wider Nigerian political community, where he served with dedication and contributed meaningfully to the development of Delta State and our country,” he said. Obaseki recalled Uduaghan’s Delta Beyond Oil initiative, which sought to diversify the state’s economy, as well as his efforts to promote the welfare of residents and regional cooperation among South-South states. He said the former governor’s contributions to public service and the relationships he built would remain part of his legacy. Obaseki extended his condolences to the bereaved family and the government and people of Delta State, praying God to grant the deceased eternal rest. His legacies live on — Iyovwaye Iyovwaye said he received the news of Uduaghan’s death with a heavy heart, describing the former governor as an elder brother with whom he shared a relationship built on mutual respect. He said Uduaghan devoted many years to public service, first as secretary to the state government and later as governor from 2007 to 2015. According to Iyovwaye, the former governor’s administration would be remembered for the Delta Beyond Oil initiative and contributions to healthcare, education, infrastructure and human capital development. “Beyond politics, he was a medical doctor, a leader, and a proud son of Delta State who dedicated a significant part of his life to serving our people,” he said. Iyovwaye added that his relationship with Uduaghan went beyond political affiliations, saying he would cherish their conversations and the mutual respect they shared. He extended his condolences to Uduaghan’s wife, children, the wider family, the Itsekiri nation and the people of Delta State, praying God to grant them the strength to bear the loss and the deceased eternal rest. items.title: 2027: Wike’s political calculations have shaped Rivers politics — APC chieftain
items.description: Dike hails rapprochement with Fubara By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Princewill Dike, has described the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, as the “political Chike Obi of Rivers State,” citing his political calculations, strategic manoeuvres and ability to win elections. Dike, a Port Harcourt-based lawyer and political commentator, said on Tuesday that Wike had demonstrated an understanding of Rivers politics, adding that his influence and ability to build political alliances had continued to shape the state’s political landscape. Dike recalled that in 2014, he watched a television appearance on the African Independent Television (AIT) in which former Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Henry Odein Ajumogobia, SAN, reportedly expressed interest in contesting the 2015 Rivers State governorship election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with the expectation that Wike would support his ambition. According to Dike, Ajumogobia was said to have withdrawn from the race after Wike declared his governorship ambition, reportedly acknowledging Wike’s political understanding as comparable to his own knowledge of the law. Dike said the episode reinforced his conviction that Wike possessed an uncommon grasp of political strategy, which distinguished him among political actors in Rivers State. He recalled that following Wike’s victory over the political camp of former Governor Rotimi Amaechi in the 2015 governorship election, he described the FCT minister as the political “wizard of Rivers State”, a nickname he said reflected Wike’s political influence and strategic approach. Dike said the description of Wike as the political Chike Obi of Rivers State was also appropriate, given what he characterised as the minister’s “ingenious political permutations, calculations and ability to navigate complex political situations”. His latest assessment followed developments involving Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective supporters, whom he described as an extended family of political stakeholders in the state. Dike welcomed the apparent rapprochement between the two political leaders and their supporters, describing it as a significant step towards reconciliation and unity in Rivers State. The APC chieftain attributed Wike’s continued political relevance not only to his strategic calculations but also to what he described as his generosity and willingness to forgive former political associates with whom he had disagreements. According to him, Wike’s reported readiness to welcome former adversaries back into his political fold without dwelling on past disagreements had helped him sustain relationships and consolidate his influence. Dike, who has consistently advocated political reconciliation in Rivers State, said the latest development supported his earlier position that the disagreements would eventually give way to renewed cooperation. He expressed hope that the development would create an opportunity for political stakeholders to work together and usher in a period of greater understanding and cooperation in the state. “The development is the beginning of a new political chapter in Rivers State. The apparent rapprochement had given me reasons to celebrate. Rivers State is now moving towards becoming one political family,” he said. Dike also praised Wike’s willingness to forgive former associates, navigate political challenges and rebuild relationships, arguing that these qualities had contributed to his standing in Rivers politics and his description of the minister as the “father of Rivers politics”. items.title: Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill has concluded the drafting phase of its assignment and formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), alongside 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative review and validation. The submission was made on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation, AGF and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan. This was revealed via a statement issued by the Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila. Gbajabiamila, who was a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, explained that the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws. According to the statement: “The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate. “The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.” He further said: “The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly. “The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.” The post Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Judicial funding and operational reforms needed to speed up justice delivery – Yaw Nsarkoh
items.description: The former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has called for improved resourcing and a comprehensive operational review of Ghana’s judicial system, arguing that adding more judges alone will not resolve the challenges affecting justice delivery. He says the country must examine how cases move through the courts, identify the causes of delays and deploy technology and better planning to improve efficiency. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event on Tuesday, October 20, he said meaningful reform would require funding, but stressed that the management of existing resources was equally important. Mr Nsarkoh cited what he described as Ghana’s limited capacity to finance its development priorities, arguing that the economy was too small to meet the competing demands of a population of about 34 million people. He urged the involvement of experienced planners and operations managers in assessing the judicial process from beginning to end. “We must get seasoned planners and operations managers to look at the end-to-end judicial process, with a view to optimising service to citizens,” he said. Mr Nsarkoh suggested that professional bodies, including the Ghana Institution of Engineering and organisations representing project managers and planners, could contribute to the review. He also questioned whether the large number of land disputes clogging the judicial system should prompt broader reforms in land administration rather than a response focused primarily on increasing the number of judges. He identified other recurring disputes, including those connected to funerals and chieftaincy, as problems that society must address at their roots instead of continually relying on an under-resourced court system. Mr Nsarkoh further urged the judiciary to embrace technology to improve its operations, arguing that properly deployed tools could expand institutional capacity. He maintained that without adequate funding, systematic problem-solving and improved operational management, calls for judicial reform would remain largely aspirational.

items.title: Presidency targets ₦20bn to tackle climate change in North West, holds summit in Abuja
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Presidency on Tuesday said it is seeking to mobilise about ₦20 billion over the next four years to confront flooding, drought, desertification, migration and other climate pressures across the region. This is as the North-West Climate Summit has been described as Africa’s first regional climate marketplace. Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-West), Hon. Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, said the summit is the inaugural edition of a regional platform designed to connect states and local governments with development partners, financial institutions and investors. The initiative is being implemented with the Northern Governors’ Forum, the North-West Governors’ Forum and the North-West Development Commission. Yakasai said the summit rests on three pillars: a Climate Marketplace, a Climate Academy and a Climate Fund. He explained that the marketplace will allow subnational governments to showcase climate programmes and attract partnerships and financing from local and international institutions. “Local governments and states can go into that platform and put up what they are doing on climate change, so that international development partners, international financial institutions, and even the local ones can see what programmes they are doing on climate,” he said. He explained that the Climate Academy is expected to train 10,000 young people across the North-West on climate resilience, climate action and related areas. According to him, the Climate Fund will channel resources towards interventions on flooding, drought, renewable energy and other climate-related challenges. “That fund will be channelled through the Office of the SSA on Community Engagement to tackle those issues,” Yakasai said. The presidential aide said organisers are targeting about N20 billion over the next four years to support climate interventions in the region. “We are looking at the region of N20 billion in the next four years,” he said. “All these are aimed at easing the problems of climate, because this is what is bedevilling the whole world.” He said the initiative builds on work that began last year and is intended to strengthen Nigeria’s position ahead of the forthcoming United Nations Climate Change Summit. “We want to take up what we have gotten here, the discussions we have had here, because we have had a lot of interactive sessions,” Yakasai said. “We take it up and see where we can match our strength with what we can see at the international climate change summit that is coming up.” Yakasai identified flooding, migration, drought, dry-season pressures and the need for renewable energy as major challenges facing the North-West. “Anything that has to do with climate challenge, we focus on it and see how we can help in alleviating those challenges,” he said. The summit is positioned as an investment-focused platform for climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy, water security and youth-led green enterprises across Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara states. Yakasai said the regional approach is significant because it moves climate action beyond individual state projects into a coordinated platform for financing, capacity-building and implementation. The seven states of the North West Kano, Kaduna, Kebbi, Katsina, Sokoto, Jigawa and Zamfara states sent their representatives. The post Presidency targets ₦20bn to tackle climate change in North West, holds summit in Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Environnement des affaires : Benalilou met en garde contre l'opacité des procédures comme vecteur de corruption
items.description: Le président de l'Instance nationale de la probité, de la prévention et de la lutte contre la corruption (INPPLC), Mohammed Benalilou, a tiré la sonnette d'alarme sur les risques que fait peser l'opacité administrative sur le tissu économique. S'exprimant ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 lors d'une rencontre à Rabat consacrée au « Comportement responsable des entreprises au Maroc : levier stratégique de durabilité et de compétitivité » , il a souligné que l'insécurité procédurale face aux entreprises alimente directement la corruption et ouvre la voie aux marchandages, menaçant la confiance des investisseurs et la pérennité du climat des affaires. Le président de l'INPPLC a également rappelé que la corruption ne constitue pas simplement un risque juridique et pénal, mais porte une atteinte directe à la réputation de l'entreprise, à ses relations commerciales ainsi qu'à la confiance de ses partenaires. En fragilisant la capacité de survie des entités économiques, elle étouffe l'innovation et altère la qualité des services. Dès lors, a-t-il dit, l'investissement dans la probité s'impose comme un gage de durabilité et de stabilité. Toutefois, Mohammed Benalilou a refusé de faire porter cette responsabilité aux seules entreprises, affirmant que l'adoption d'un comportement responsable exige un cadre institutionnel incitatif. Les autorités publiques et les institutions nationales se doivent de garantir un environnement transparent, juste et prévisible, où les critères d'octroi des autorisations, d'attribution des marchés, d'accès aux subventions et les délais de recours sont clairement fixés pour limiter le pouvoir d'appréciation discrétionnaire, a-t-il indiqué en ce sens. Pour le président de l'Instance, la probité dépasse la simple conformité formelle ou l'adoption de chartes déconnectées des réalités opérationnelles. Elle doit s'ériger en véritable mode de gouvernance stratégique et en culture organisationnelle intégrée à tous les niveaux de décision, depuis le choix des fournisseurs jusqu'à la gestion des conflits d'intérêts et le respect des engagements sociaux et environnementaux. Appelant à dépasser la multiplication de mécanismes purement techniques pour privilégier une volonté politique réelle au sein des instances dirigeantes, Mohammed Benalilou a réaffirmé la nécessité de promouvoir des alertes éthiques protégées et des cartes de risques effectives, condition sine qua non pour passer d'une conformité de façade à une probité réelle et opérationnelle. © Mounir Mehimdate A noter que la séance d'ouverture de cette rencontre a été marquée par la signature de mémorandums d'entente entre l'Agence Marocaine de Développement des Investissements et des Exportations (AMDIE) et cinq partenaires institutionnels et économiques, à savoir l'INPPLC, l'Agence Nationale de Gestion Stratégique des Participations de l’État (ANGSPE), la Confédération générale des entreprises du Maroc (CGEM), l'Association marocaine des industries du textile et de l'habillement (AMITH) et la Fédération nationale de l'agroalimentaire (FENAGRI). Ces partenariats visent à renforcer la coopération entre les acteurs publics et privés et à promouvoir des initiatives conjointes en faveur de la conduite responsable des entreprises. Ils traduisent une ambition commune de placer la gouvernance, l'intégrité et la durabilité au cœur de la transformation économique du Royaume, au service de la compétitivité, de l'attractivité des investissements et d'une croissance durable. The post Environnement des affaires : Benalilou met en garde contre l'opacité des procédures comme vecteur de corruption appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Yaw Nsarkoh questions relevance of palanquin tradition, calls for cultural rethinking
items.description: Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the continued practice of carrying chiefs in palanquins, challenging Ghanaians to examine whether every cultural tradition remains beneficial in a changing society. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Nsarkoh said the practice illustrated the need to question long-standing customs and consider when modifications become necessary for progressive innovation. He recounted watching a video of a chief dancing in a palanquin carried by young men, questioning whether the practice should automatically be defended as culture. “Our larger society continues to allow young men to carry dancing chiefs on their heads in palanquins and call that culture,” he said. He described the scene as an example of a tradition that, in his view, deserved closer examination. “Why this manual palanquin is required in the final quarter of the 27th year of the 21st century is simply incomprehensible to me. But it is a useful illustration of what can go wrong when professions refuse to examine themselves critically,” he said. Mr Nsarkoh’s remarks formed part of a broader critique of professional culture in Ghana, particularly what he described as the legal profession’s resistance to critical self-examination. He said he had been fascinated by the profession’s attachment to ritual and tradition but was more concerned about rigid hierarchies and age-based discrimination. “I am more concerned about the rigid hierarchy that comes close to a professional variety of gerontocratic feudalism, which is so brazenly on display sometimes,” he said. He also questioned the practice of arranging court cases according to the seniority of lawyers, often justified on the grounds that junior lawyers learn by observing more experienced practitioners. “That sort of thing in my view needs to be modified,” he said. Mr Nsarkoh argued that technological advances could make it easier to schedule court cases in ways that allow lawyers to plan their work while creating more opportunities for professional development. He said younger lawyers should have greater freedom to decide which experienced practitioners they wished to observe in court, rather than having their learning opportunities determined primarily by seniority. “Age and experience must be respected, but by themselves they prove nothing,” he stated.

items.title: Otti, Wabara mourn Prof Greg Ibe, Uduaghan
items.description: Gregory University declares seven days of mourning for founder By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, and former Senate President, Senator Adolphus Wabara, have mourned the deaths of Professor Gregory Ikechukwu Ibe, founder of Gregory University, Uturu, and former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Otti and Wabara described Ibe’s death as a major loss to Abia State and Nigeria, while Wabara also paid tribute to Uduaghan’s contributions to governance and public service. Their tributes came as Gregory University declared seven days of mourning in honour of its founder and proprietor, who died following health challenges. Ibe, a professor of entrepreneurial management and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) governorship candidate in the 2023 election, was also a recipient of the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR). In a condolence message issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, Otti said he received the news of Ibe’s death with shock and sadness, recalling his contributions to education and research, particularly in Abia State. The governor said he had hoped and prayed that the late professor, who had battled an illness for some time, would recover. “Unfortunately, he couldn’t. We cannot question God,” Otti said. He urged the deceased’s family, friends and associates to draw strength from the life he lived and the legacies he left behind, appealing to them not to “mourn like those without hope”. On behalf of his family, the Abia State Government and the people of the state, Otti commiserated with the bereaved family and prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul. Wabara: Abia, Ndigbo lost a rare gem Similarly, Wabara described Ibe’s death as a monumental loss to Abia State, Ndigbo and Nigeria, saying the late professor was one of Abia’s finest personalities whose impact on society would endure. Wabara said he received the news of Ibe’s demise with rude shock and utter disbelief, adding that his contributions to education, philanthropy and human development, as well as his positive impact on countless lives, would remain legendary. He said the late university founder would also be remembered for his advocacy and strong belief in the Abia Charter of Equity, which promotes power rotation in the interest of fairness and justice. The former Senate President regretted that Ibe died at a time when his services and presence were still needed, particularly as Abia continued its quest for development. He prayed God to grant the bereaved family the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. University declares seven days of mourning Meanwhile, Gregory University has declared seven days of mourning for its founder, describing his death as a major loss to the university community and the education sector. In a statement signed by the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Cele Njoku, on behalf of the university management, the institution recalled that Ibe was the driving force behind its establishment in 2012 and remained committed to expanding access to education, particularly for less-privileged Nigerians. As part of the mourning arrangements, the university directed that all flags on its campus be flown at half-mast. It also opened condolence registers at the Vice-Chancellor’s Office in the Senate Building and at its liaison offices in Abuja and Lagos. The management further announced the suspension of social and sporting activities, including preparations for the second ASTEF Torch Run. It appealed to Nigerians, parents, students, alumni, the National Universities Commission and the wider academic community to pray for the peaceful repose of Ibe’s soul and for strength for his immediate family and the university community. The late professor is survived by six children and seven grandchildren. The university said funeral arrangements would be announced in due course, in line with the position of his royal family. Wabara mourns former Delta governor, Uduaghan In a separate condolence message, Wabara, who is the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), mourned the death of Uduaghan, describing it as a painful loss to Delta State, the South-South region and Nigeria. The former Senate President said Uduaghan’s contributions to governance and public service would remain part of his enduring legacy, noting that his death would be deeply felt by his family, political associates and the people of Delta State. Wabara said Uduaghan made indelible marks as governor of Delta State under the PDP. He extended his sympathies to the Uduaghan family and the government and people of Delta State, praying God to grant the bereaved family the strength to bear the loss and grant the deceased eternal rest. items.title: 2027: Atiku’ll cut cost of living, revive Eastern ports — Akobundu
items.description: Senator inaugurates grassroots support group in two Abia LGAs By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Senator Austin Akobundu, Director-General and Campaign Manager of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign for former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, has said an Atiku presidency would reduce the cost of living, revive the economy and reactivate the Eastern maritime port corridor. Akobundu spoke during the inauguration of the Atiku/Akobundu Vanguard, a grassroots support group, in Osisioma Ngwa and Isiala Ngwa North Local Government Areas of Abia State. He blamed the economic hardship in the country on the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that Atiku had the experience and economic blueprint to reverse the trend. According to him, Atiku’s proposed targeted and transparent fuel subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of food, housing, education and other essential goods and services. “President Tinubu’s policies have pushed Nigerians into unprecedented hardship and made us the poverty capital of the world,” Akobundu said. He added, “But Atiku Abubakar comes with the experience, compassion and competence to reverse this decline. He will make Nigeria affordable, productive and respected again.” The senator also identified the reactivation of the Eastern maritime port corridor as a key component of Atiku’s proposed economic agenda for the South-East. He said reviving the corridor would expand access to international trade, stimulate industrial activity, create jobs and strengthen the region’s economic base. “Atiku has a clear, actionable plan to revive the economy of the South-East alongside every other region. With the Atiku Abubakar/Rotimi Amaechi ticket, no region will be left behind,” he said. Akobundu described Atiku as a detribalised leader with the experience and national outlook required to unite the country, adding that his appointment as campaign director-general reflected the former vice-president’s commitment to inclusiveness. The inauguration attracted ADC leaders, party candidates, community elders, youth groups, women leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the two local government areas and other parts of Abia Central. Akobundu highlights constituency projects The senator, who is also the ADC candidate for Abia Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, used the occasion to highlight his legislative and constituency interventions in Osisioma Ngwa and Isiala Ngwa North. On legislation, he cited bills seeking the establishment of a Federal Institute of Entrepreneurship and Technical Skills Development in Osisioma and a National Sports University at Nsulu in Isiala Ngwa North. He also listed youth empowerment initiatives, including free training for more than 400 secondary school students in robotics, artificial intelligence and embedded systems engineering. Other programmes, according to him, included digital skills training for 360 youths, training for 400 youths in cosmetics production and paint-making, and support for 100 youths trained in farming and tailoring. He said beneficiaries of the farming and tailoring programme received sewing machines, start-up kits and financial support, while those trained in cosmetics production and paint-making received cash grants to establish businesses. In education, Akobundu said he had paid ₦21 million in scholarships for 113 constituents at the Nigeria Teachers Institute, while 114 students in tertiary institutions received grants of ₦200,000 each. He also cited medical outreaches, the installation of solar streetlights in markets across the two local government areas, solar-powered boreholes and school renovation projects among his interventions. The projects, he said, included the renovation of Immaculate Girls’ Secondary School and the construction of a skills acquisition centre. He added that work was ongoing on a classroom block at Ntigha Primary School. He listed the completion of Ihie Health Centre, renovation of Obikabia and Mbubo primary schools, and electrification of Isiala Amapu Ntigha Autonomous Community among projects planned for the future. Woos Osisioma stakeholders Akobundu and his entourage later visited political leaders and other stakeholders from Osisioma Ngwa at the residence of Chief Solomon Adaelu, where he sought their support for Atiku’s presidential ambition and his own senatorial bid. He urged the stakeholders to support Atiku, expressing confidence that the former vice-president could steer the country away from its current economic difficulties. Those present included the Director-General of the Akobundu Campaign Council, Elder Sam Njoku; members of the campaign team; ADC candidates in the two local government areas; and associates of the senator. items.title: Yaw Nsarkoh urges professionals, media to shift focus from partisan fights to national development
items.description: The former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has challenged Ghana’s professional class and media organisations to move beyond partisan disputes and focus more on the country’s development challenges, arguing that professional success must translate into improved living conditions for citizens. He says professionals who have acquired knowledge, influence and leadership positions have a responsibility to help address the social and economic conditions affecting the wider population. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event on Tuesday, October 20, he argued that the purpose of professional practice should not be separated from society’s broader development needs. Drawing on the words of American writer Toni Morrison, Mr Nsarkoh said people who had attained positions of influence should use their opportunities to empower others. He maintained that the responsibility was particularly urgent in societies where poverty, inequality and injustice continued to limit the prospects of many citizens. “It is difficult to see how we can define a serious and meaningful purpose for the existence of any profession if its key outcomes are decoupled from moving society forward,” he said. Mr Nsarkoh criticised what he described as the dominance of partisan arguments in national conversations, saying discussions about how to improve society had increasingly given way to political blame games. He also challenged the media to reconsider its emphasis on partisan confrontations and personalities at the expense of substantive discussions about development. He argued that the country needed more sustained engagement on how to improve livelihoods, strengthen institutions and create opportunities for people living in poverty. Mr Nsarkoh also warned that widespread deprivation could undermine social stability, insisting that the long-term security of the wealthy could not be separated from the wellbeing of the wider population. “The best solution to securing the long-term health of society that leads to peace, harmony and stability is to ensure that the popular classes can live in dignity,” he said. He urged professionals, institutions and citizens to contribute more seriously to building a society grounded in dignity, development, freedom and justice.

items.title: Police arrest six suspected robbers in Jigawa
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang allegedly responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables were stolen. The command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday. He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026. According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2 a.m., stealing ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables. He added that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they allegedly stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper. Shiisu said detectives from the Jahun Police Division launched an investigation that led to the arrest of five suspects. He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35. The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of the Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market. The suspect, identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was allegedly found with 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash. Shiisu said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation. According to him, Yusuf confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents. He added that further investigations linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to property allegedly stolen during the attacks. The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property. The post Police arrest six suspected robbers in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana makes significant progress in incorporating ESG in financial sector – Absa Bank Financial Markets Index
items.description: Ghana has made significant progress in incorporating environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations in its financial sector in recent years, according to the Absa Bank Financial Markets Index (ABFMI) 2026. The Ghana Sustainable Banking Principles (2019) encouraged banks to integrate ESG considerations into lending, risk management, and governance. The Ghana Stock Exchange’s ESG Disclosures Guidance Manual (2022) also established a common framework for identifying, measuring, and reporting ESG impacts under the Global Reporting Initiative Standards. In addition, its revised Sustainability Disclosure Guidance Manual, launched in August 2026, adds double-materiality guidance aligned with IFRS S1/S2. The ABFMI said the Ghanaian banking regulation has also expanded beyond sustainability reporting to prudential ESG-risk management. “The Bank of Ghana’s Climate-Related Financial Risk Directive requires regulated institutions to incorporate climate-related financial risks into governance and risk-management systems. Together, these developments reposition ESG from primarily a corporate social responsibility concern to an issue of financial materiality and risk management”. Ghana has established a legal framework supporting the enforceability of netting arrangements. A key development is the Banks and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Act, which recognises netting arrangements in respect of eligible financial contracts. The International Capital Market Association published its legal opinion on Ghana in 2024, confirming the validity of the Global Master Repurchase Agreement and the enforceability of itsclose-out netting provisions under Ghanaian law. The focus now is on deepening this framework, including encouraging greater use of standard master agreements such as the GMRA and Global Master Securities Lending Agreement, providing greater legal certainty for repurchase agreement and securities lending transactions and their associated close-out netting provisions.
